author: LAMA
title: Ireland: Pre-Budget Protest
content:
The Irish Left held a protest recently in anticipation of the upcoming budget. The article discusses the overall situation in Ireland and explores the nature of the protest.

Donald Trump visited Ireland recently. It was a two-day visit so he could play golf. The estimated cost to the Irish taxpayer is reported to be in excess of 20 million Euros (Clare Echo, 6/8/26). Not surprisingly, the visit caused controversy and resulted in mass protests. The latter is a good thing. What is strange, however, was the lack of enthusiasm for a protest held just one week later in Dublin.

A protest was called for September 19 th in Parnell Square, Central Dublin, as a pre-Budget demonstration. The budget is due to be announced on October 6 th by Finance Minister Simon Harris on behalf of the right-wing coalition of Fianna Fail and Fine Gael. The government is sitting on a surplus, but indications are they intend to do little or nothing to help those in need of support.

There are a number of basic issues that highlight a social crisis in the 26 Counties. A big one is housing. Social housing is no longer being built people are waiting years on lists and private landlords are allowed to get away with exorbitant rents. It is not unusual for people to pay 40 or 50% of their income on rent. That’s if you can actually find somewhere in the first place. Many young people are living in the bedrooms they grew up in, since availability is as much a problem as affordability. Outright homelessness is on the rise too. The Department of Housing figures show that those in emergency housing increased 9.1% over the year to July 2026 (RTE 28/8/26). Among those was a 16% increase in families (Focus Ireland 28/8/26).

The problem does not only occur on a national level. The grassroots housing campaign group Community Action Tenants’ Union (CATU) is battling against Dublin City Council. Council executives have increased rents for tenants in public housing, the excuse being that there isn’t money to keep public housing in reasonable condition, so it will have to come out of rent increases. The increase voted on in April offers no exemptions for pensioners, people on welfare, or disability recipients. For many of those groups dependent on fixed incomes, any increase will further diminish their quality of life.

Besides housing, another concern is basic resource infrastructure. Due to extremely hot weather conditions, a hosepipe ban was enforced between July and the middle of September in the Greater Dublin Area, and parts of Wexford, Wicklow, Meath, Kildare and south Tipperary.

Uisce Eireann (UE) is the state-owned company that was responsible for overseeing the ban. UE declared the prohibition “…for activities including watering gardens, washing private vehicles and leisure boats, filling domestic swimming or paddling pools, ornamental fountains and garden ponds except where such use is required for commercial purposes [emphasis added]”, (RTE, 22/7/26). In other words, business got a pass and the average person had to toe the line.

Although UE is a state company, it is in fact structured as a commercial semi-state company with share holders. The two shareholders are government ministers. It is clear from all this whose interests are seen to take priority. It is not the people at the bottom.

In addition, electricity prices are rising. Several suppliers have announced increases, with some already taking effect and others about to. For example, SSE Airtricity is increasing electricity rates by 9.4% from October 5 th , with the typical bill rising by about 8.9% or 172 Euros a year (The Irish Times, 4/9/26). Another is Pinergy, which imposed a 7.6% increase (RTE 14/8/26). The result is on a straight Euro-per-kWh measure, Ireland now has the highest electricity costs in the European Union (EU), at about 40% above the EU average! (ec.europa.eu). While the average person is clearly struggling to pay these increases, data centres and big tech companies (with the latter only paying 12.5% tax) pay wholesale rates for their water and electricity, while using a huge percentage of the national consumption. Its not too hard to see who the state favours.

Examples could be multiplied across various other aspects of the cost-of-living crisis. One such being a 15% increase in public transport, announced to take place from January (thejournal.ie 3/9/26).Many working people rely on buses and trains to commute to work, and such increases only add to the burden we face …

author: Unknown
title: La mobilisation lycéenne continue !
content:
Hier, certains lycées de l'agglomération lyonnaise rejoignaient la forte mobilisation lycéenne initiée depuis la région parisienne la semaine dernière. Prenant la suite d'un mouvement printanier qui a marqué le ministère, les flics et les esprits malgré sa courte durée, le mouvement s'est amplifié et a touché presque 200 lycées sur le territoire, des Alpes Maritimes à Lille en passant par Marseille et Grenoble.


Les raisons des blocages initiés autour de la mobilisation des élèves du lycée Saint-Exupéry de Créteil (Ile-de-France) sont nombreuses et variées : manque de moyens, surcharge chronique des classes, locaux délabrés, coûts de cantine, cours de 8h à 18h, manque de personnel, profs, infirmier-es, assitantes sociales et

AESH

 et des appels plus larges contre le fascisme et la guerre par certaines franges du mouvement.


Lundi 28 septembre, quatre lycées, Jean-Paul-Sartre à (Bron), Charlie-Chaplin (Décines-Charpieu), Robert-Doisneau à (Vaulx-en-Velin) et Frédéric-Faÿs (Villeurbanne), ont été bloqués. La répression policière, annoncée en grande pompe par le ministère de l'éducation nationale et par la préfecture a été particulièrement violente autour des établissements, envoyant plusieurs élèves à l'hôpital à Villeurbanne et mettant de nombreux autres en garde-à-vue ce, sans que les familles ne soient même prévenues. Les flics seraient aussi rentrés dans le lycée Doisneau à Vaulx-en-Velin en marge du blocage.


Dans une tentative lâche de casser la dynamique du mouvement, les administrations des lycées Faÿs et Jean-Paul Satre ont annulé les cours toute la journée du 28 septembre et l'inspection académique a carrément pris les commandes du lycée Faÿs en annulant tous les cours jusqu'à jeudi. Une manière bien peu discrète de ne pas assumer la réplique annoncée du fait d'avoir réprimé aussi violemment les lycéen-nes et d'en avoir emmené autant au comico.


La répression orchestrée par le ministère de l'intérieur main dans la main avec les inspections académiques a au total menée à l'arrestation de 164 personnes et blessé un grand nombre de lycéen-nes, que ce soit par gazage, tabassages ou tirs de

LBD

.


 Répression féroce contre des blocages dans 4 lycées


 Quatre lycées de l'agglomération ont été bloqués par des lycéen-nes ce matin avant de se faire réprimer violemment par les flics.


 29 septembre


Un certain nombre d'appels circulent pour continuer et amplifier le mouvement aujourd'hui, continuons à soutenir les lycéen-nes

 

!

author: CMI Argentina
title: “Las protestas y las luchas en las que participaron Milton y Eneas no son terrorismo”
content:
La Coordinadora contra la Represión Policial e Institucional (CORREPI) y la Gremial de Abogados reclaman el cierre de la causa contra Milton Iván Tolomeo y Eneas Germán Gallo Salomone Croft, detenidos por haber participado de la masiva protesta ante el Congreso de la Nación contra la regresiva reforma laboral.


Compartimos el comunicado de CORREPI y la Gremial de Abogados:


LAS PROTESTAS Y LAS LUCHAS EN QUE PARTICIPARON MILTON Y ENEAS NO SON TERRORISMO LIBERTAD A MILTON Y ENEAS, CIERRE DE LA CAUSA.


El 11 de febrero de 2026 el Congreso Nacional perpetró un verdadero crimen al sancionar la llamada Ley de Reforma Laboral, que destruyó 200 años de derechos conquistados por las y los trabajadores de Argentina. Ese día hubo una masiva movilización en la Plaza de los Dos Congresos, con la participación de las centrales sindicales, infinidad de gremios y multitud de personas que manifestaron su repudio a lo que sucedía en el recinto.


Unos días después, varias personas que fueron “identificadas” a través de dudosos mecanismos de ciberpatrullaje y reconocimiento facial resultaron detenidas, acusadas de graves delitos por haber participado de la manifestación multitudinaria.


Desde mediados de febrero, dos trabajadores, Milton Iván Tolomeo y Eneas Germán Gallo Salomone Croft, están detenidos en la prisión federal de Marcos Paz. A la vez, Oscar Rubén “Homero” Aguirre y Néstor Gabriel Barrera fueron detenidos y excarcelados, pero siguen procesados en la misma causa.


Cuando Milton fue detenido, se lo incluyó, por orden del Ministerio de Seguridad Nacional, en el SIGGPLAR (Sistema Integral de Gestión para Personas Privadas de la Libertad de Alto Riesgo), destinado a terroristas de gran peligrosidad, lo que significó un aislamiento absoluto, sin posibilidad de comunicarse ni tener visitas de sus familiares ni de sus defensores, con apenas una o dos horas de recreo para poder salir de su celda, usar los baños, comer o salir al patio, vigilado en todo momento por personal no identificado del Servicio Penitenciario Federal enmascarado con balaclavas.


Logramos, al mes, sacarlo de ese infierno y lograr su pase a un pabellón común.


Se los acusa por los delitos de tenencia de material incendiario, atentado y resistencia a la autoridad e intimidación pública, Milton y Eneas como coutores y Homero y Néstor como partícipes.


Como si eso fuera poco, ya esa acusación prevé la pena de 5 a 15 años de prisión, el Fiscal Stornelli requirió el agregado del agravante previsto en el art. 41 quinquies del Código Penal, que establece la duplicación de penas cuando el hecho se comete “para aterrorizar a la población u obligar a autoridades públicas nacionales, gobiernos extranjeros o agentes internacionales a realizar un acto o abstenerse de hacerlo”.


Este artículo fue incorporado al Código Penal en 2011 (ley 26.734), como parte de la batería de “leyes antiterroristas” dictadas a partir de 2007 por presión del GAFI (Grupo de Acción Financiera Internacional) y otros organismos internacionales de control financiero, y fue ampliado aún más en 2024 con la ley 27.739. Es una circunstancia agravante transversal a todo el Código Penal, que automáticamente lleva al doble la escala penal prevista, sin respetar el criterio de proporcionalidad de la pena.


Tanto al momento de su sanción inicial durante la presidencia de Cristina Fernández, como ante su reforma en la actual gestión de Javier Milei, desde las organizaciones populares y sectores académicos advertimos que es una norma peligrosísima, plagada de vaguedades, con expresiones completamente abiertas a la interpretación, como “aterrorizar a la población”, cuya definición queda discrecionalmente en manos de jueces y fiscales que decidan descargar todo su poder punitivo apuntando más a presuntas intencionalidades subjetivas del autor que a las características concretas de una conducta específica.


Decíamos también que, aunque la misma norma indica que esa agravante no se debe aplicar cuando los hechos de que se trate tuvieran lugar “en ocasión del ejercicio de derechos humanos y/o sociales o de cualquier otro derecho constitucional”, como es el de resistir una medida legislativa que cercena derechos, la falta de precisión de las definiciones que permiten cualquier interpretación intencionada de jueces y fiscales obedientes al poder político habilitan la indiscriminada persecución de la protesta y su híper criminalización.


Desde el inicio de la gestión del gobierno de la Libertad Avanza …

author: Unknown
title: Hozat'ta kadınların öncülüğünde uyuşturucu karşıtı yürüyüş: Uyuşturucu ve çeteleşmeye izin vermeyeceğiz
content:
Dersim – Hozat Kent Meclisi’nin çağrısıyla ilçede uyuşturucuya ve çeteleşmeye karşı yürüyüş ve basın açıklaması gerçekleştirildi. Açıklamada, “Bizim mücadelemiz gençlerimizin uyuşturucudan, çeteleşmeden ve her türlü bağımlılık ilişkisinden korunması içindir” denildi.

Hozat Kent Meclisi tarafından düzenlenen yürüyüş ve basın açıklamasında “Uyuşturucu ve çeteleşmeye izin vermeyeceğiz, gençlik bizimdir kaybetmeyeceğiz” pankartı taşındı. Kadınların öncülüğünde yapılan yürüyüşte "Dersim Gençliği Yalnız Değildir", "Hozat Sahipsiz Değildir" sloganları atıldı.

Hazırlanan basın açıklamasını Sabit Menteşe okudu.

Menteşe, Hozat’ta uzun süredir tüm toplumun ortak kaygısı olan sorunlara karşı bir şeyler yapmanın, susmak yerine konuşmanın, seyretmek yerine sorumluluk almanın gereğine inanarak yola çıktıklarını belirterek, yakın zamanda Kent Meclisi yürütmesinde görev alan Hıdır Dilekçi'nin evinin önünde saldırıya uğradığını hatırlattı.

Saldırıyı açık ve kesin bir biçimde kınadıklarını söyleyen Menteşe, “Ancak burada asıl mesele yalnızca Hıdır Dilekçi’ye yönelik saldırı değildir. Asıl mesele, Hozatta toplumun ortak iradesini ortaya koymaya çalışan insanlara korku salınmak istenmesidir. Eğer amaç bir gözdağı vermekse yanlış kapıyı çaldınız. Bu saldırılar bizi yıldırmayacaktır. Tam tersine, doğru bir yerde durduğumuzu ve daha fazla dayanışmaya, daha fazla örgütlü toplumsal iradeye ihtiyaç olduğunu bir kez daha göstermiştir” dedi.

Menteşe, “Kimse bizden susmamızı beklemesin. Kimse Hozat’ın sokaklarının, meydanlarının ve ortak yaşam alanlarının birkaç kendini bilmezin korku alanına dönüşmesine razı olmamızı beklemesin. Meydanı birkaç kendini bilmeze teslim etmeyeceğiz. Bu mücadelenin temel sloganı haline gelen 'Hozat sahipsiz değildir’i bundan daha güçlü şekilde haykıracağız. Hozat çocuklarıyla, gençleriyle, kadınlarıyla, yaşlılarıyla, esnafıyla, emekçisiyle ve bütün yurttaşlarıyla bizim ortak yaşam alanımızdır” ifadelerini kullandı. “Mücadelemiz gençlerimiz için”

Mücadelelerinin herhangi bir kişiye karşı değil; gençlerin uyuşturucudan, çeteleşmeden ve her türlü bağımlılık ilişkisinden korunması için olduğunu söyleyen Menteşe, şunları kaydetti: "Bizim mücadelemiz çocuklarımızın güven içinde büyüyebileceği, insanların birbirinden korkmadan yaşayabileceği bir Hozat içindir. Bizim mücadelemiz sorunların üzerinin örtülmediği, konuşulabildiği ve çözüm için herkesin sorumluluk aldığı bir Hozat içindir. Biz korkuya karşı cesareti, yalnızlığa karşı dayanışmayı, suskunluğa karşı sözü büyüteceğiz. Çünkü biliyoruz ki Hozat’ın geleceği korkuya değil, Hozat halkının ortak iradesine aittir. Hozat sahipsiz değildir. Korkmuyoruz, susmuyoruz, geri adım atmayacağız. Hozat’ı korkuya teslim etmeyeceğiz."

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Appel à se mobiliser et à manifester pour la libre circulation et contre les frontières et l'enfermement le 4 octobre à 14h place de la comédie à Montpellier.
content:
Adissiatz ! Nous sommes une interorga de collectifs et de personnes s'organisant contre les frontières et l'enfermement dans les pays d'oc, des Pyrénées aux Alpes en passant par la Méditerranée, à la croisée des états français, italien et espagnol. Nous vous invitons à nous rejoindre pour une manifestation le 4 octobre à Montpellier pour lutter contre le continuum colonial entre frontières, enfermement et fabrique de l'illégalité. Nous souhaitons la disparition des frontières et la libre circulation pour toustes ! RDV à 14h à la comédie !


Adissiatz ! Nous sommes une interorga de collectifs et de personnes s'organisant contre les frontières et l'enfermement dans les pays d'oc, des Pyrénées aux Alpes en passant par la Méditerranée, à la croisée des états français, italien et espagnol. Nous vous invitons à nous rejoindre pour une manifestation le 4 octobre à Montpellier pour lutter contre le continuum colonial entre frontières, enfermement et fabrique de l'illégalité. Nous souhaitons la disparition des frontières et la libre circulation pour toustes ! RDV à 14h à la comédie !


Depuis le hangar d'Arenc à Marseille dans les années 70, emprisonnant les algériens après leur révolution anti-coloniale, les lieux d'enfermement n'ont fait que se multiplier. CRA pour Centre de Rétention Administratif, ou une prison pour les personnes qui n'auraient pas les « bons papiers » (toulouseanticra.org). Au delà des CRA, nous militons contre toutes les entraves à la libre circulation des personnes. Frontières, prisons, hospitalisations forcées, assignations à résidence, expulsions, expropriations, accaparements de terres, ségrégation, colonisation sont des dispositifs injustes utilisant la violence pour déplacer, bloquer et enfermer les personnes contre leur volonté.


En 2023, l'état français a annoncé un doublement des places en CRA pour atteindre 3000 en 2027. A Béziers, 140 places sont prévues, à côté d'une prison de 1200 personnes (prévue pour 800) et d'un futur hopital psychiatrique, pour créer comme souvent un complexe carcéral et répressif, où transférer facilement les personnes à qui l'on vole leur liberté. Le terrain a été clôturé et mis sous vidéo-surveillance, après que nous l'ayons occupé lors de la mobilisation d'octobre 2025.


Les récentes lois européennes (Règlement retour, 2026) vont toujours plus loin dans la création de statuts de citoyenneté inférieurs. Par des entourloupes juridiques, les personnes arrivées dans l'UE sans visa ne sont pas considérees comme réellement sur le territoire, et n'ont donc pas les mêmes droits. Au delà des CRA, les personnes peuvent être enfermées dans des 'zones d'attente' jusqu'à 6 mois, puis expulsées dans des 'hubs de retour', prisons et camps construits hors de l'UE. En parallèle FRONTEX coordonne la création d'une force armée de fichage et de répression évoquant l'ICE états-unienne, et le nombre de frères et soeurs mort.es en mer et aux frontières augmente chaque jour.


Le harcèlement des personnes sans les « bons papiers » permet de réprimer et contrôler les corps minorisés, précarisant, enfermant et broyant les personnes, fabriquant par la peur et la violence une main d'oeuvre docile à bas coût pour enrichir les puissants.


La manifestation du 4 octobre est déclarée. le parcours : comédie - préfecture - arceaux... Nous vous invitons toustes à participer mais sans drapeaux d'organisations. Manifestons ensemble sous la bannière commune de la libre circulation, de la régularisation de tous les sans-papiers, de la disparition des frontières et contre les CRA !


Feu aux CRA, feu aux prisons, feu aux frontières ! Solidarité avec toutes les personnes ciblées par l'illégalité, et force à toustes celleux qui luttent à l'intérieur ! Rejoignez-nous le 4 octobre à 14h place de la Comédie à Montpellier pour résister ensemble à ce système raciste et colonial - et un jour peut-être y mettre fin.


Plus d'infos sur insta : anticra_mtp.


Contact : we_anti_CRA_3_4_octobre_2026@disroot.org.

title: People in Diyadin demonstrate against gold mining: “Killing nature means killing life”
content:
Under the slogan “We Protect Our Land,” large numbers of people demonstrated in the district of Diyadin in Ağro province against gold mining using cyanide. The environmental rally was organized by the DEM Party and the Mesopotamia Ecology Movement. The demonstrators marched from the post office on İnönü Street to the central bus terminal. Chants included “Bê ax jiyan nabe” [There is no life without land] and “Kurdistan nabe goristan” [Kurdistan will not become a graveyard.] Banners and placards carried messages including “Kurdistan is not your mining zone,” “Killing nature means killing life,” and “Hands off my air, my water, my land, and my forests.”


Participants in the rally included DBP and DEM Party co-chairs Çiğdem Kılıçgün Uçar and Tuncer Bakırhan, as well as representatives of various environmental groups. The protest was directed against a gold mining project near the village of Mollakara. Environmental organizations and municipalities in the region have warned in particular about the potential impact of cyanide use on the Murat River and its watershed.


‘We are fighting for every place that is being plundered’


Alev Yılmaz of the Varto Ecology Platform recalled the resistance against energy and resource extraction projects in Varto, which has been ongoing for more than 140 days. She stressed that the protest there was not limited to their own region: “We are waging this resistance not only for Varto, but for every place that is being plundered.”


Rojhat Özgökçe of the Mesopotamia Ecology Movement spoke of the long-standing exploitation of Kurdistan’s natural environment. At the same time, he said, the experiences in Varto and Karlıova showed that an organized ecological movement was emerging in response. “We must become stronger, organize ourselves, and develop a powerful struggle against ecocide,” Özgökçe said.


Uçar: Land is more valuable than gold


DBP (Democratic Regions Party) co-chair Çiğdem Kılıçgün Uçar linked the mining projects to poverty, migration, and the economic exploitation of the region. “Why have the people of Diyadin migrated away? Because deep poverty was left behind here,” Uçar said. She noted that attempts were now being made to bring companies into the region and exploit Diyadin. “What we must do, therefore, is protect our land. The land and the resistance of the people of Diyadin are more valuable than gold.”


She rejected claims that mining companies would bring jobs to the region: “Our people are being offered toxic employment. No one accepts the plundering of their air, water, and livelihoods. We will not accept it either.”


Uçar said that exploitation was taking place from Muş and Diyarbakır to Ağrı without regard for the people living there. “We also want to leave a dignified life for the seven-year-old children standing here in this square today.”


Uçar also called on local residents not to sell their land to mining companies: “They are trying to buy up land in the villages piece by piece. Do not sell your land.”


Ecology and peace


Referring to Abdullah Öcalan’s call of February 27, 2025, Uçar linked the protection of natural resources and ecosystems to the peace and democratic society process. “Those who do not protect their nature do not protect peace either,” the politician said. “We must begin by protecting the water and nature of this land, especially Kurdistan.” She said that companies were poised to exploit the region’s natural and social resources. “We will stand against them together in this struggle.”


Bakırhan: Kurdish population faces renewed displacement


DEM Party (Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party) co-chair Tuncer Bakırhan drew a connection between today’s mining projects and the displacement of the Kurdish population in previous decades. He recalled that millions of Kurds were forced to leave their villages, pastures, mountains, and homes as a result of war and violence in the 1990s. “Now they are trying to displace the Kurdish population for a second time through mining companies and profiteers,” Bakırhan said.


The resistance, he said, was not limited to Diyadin. “From Lice to Varto and Karlıova, and from the Ida Mountains to Akbelen Forest, people are resisting environmental destruction and profit-driven interests. We say: Do not blast our mountains, do not pollute our plains, do not pollute our water. The people will not surrender their land to companies that want to poison it, extract a little gold, and then disappear.”

title: A Year Later, Trump’s Gaza Plan Just Bought “More Time for the Genocide”
content:
Writer and analyst Muhammad Shehada notes the release of Israeli hostages is the only plan item that’s been fulfilled.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The Palestinian death toll from Israel’s war on Gaza has surpassed 74,000, according to the Ministry of Health in Gaza. While this figure represents the official death toll as confirmed by local authorities, the true number could be much higher when missing people and indirect deaths are taken into account, such as from disease, exposure, denial of medical treatment and the destruction of civic infrastructure. And since the so-called ceasefire brokered by Trump last October, nearly 1,400 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks.

“The [ceasefire] plan ended up just buying more time for the genocide,” says Muhammad Shehada, a writer and analyst from Gaza speaking to Democracy Now! in Copenhagen. “Instead of suspending attacks on Gaza, Israel has been bombing Gaza every day.”

“The idea of the plan was to divide the reconstruction, rehabilitation, Israeli withdrawal, decommissioning of Hamas and Palestinian statehood into three phases,” says Shehada. “So far, only one item of the 20 items on the Trump plan has been fulfilled, and that is the release of every single Israeli hostage in Gaza.”

title: Life of Kurdish political prisoner at risk in Tehran
content:
The Kurdistan Human Rights Network has published a report about the health of Mutelîb Ehmedyan, a Kurdish political prisoner from Rojhilat (Eastern Kurdistan).


Ehmedyan has been imprisoned for 16 years, and is reportedly suffering from several illnesses, including stomach cancer.


His health condition is said to be so serious that he is no longer fit to remain in prison. For this reason, Ehmedyan requested a postponement of the enforcement of his prison sentence. However, following an objection by the Tehran Prosecutor General’s Office, the political prisoner has continued to be held in the harsh conditions of Evin Prison.


According to the report, due to the negligence and indifference of the authorities, the Kurdish man was previously denied permission to receive treatment outside the prison. As a result, the cancer spread throughout his body. After his condition deteriorated, doctors reportedly had to remove his gallbladder, liver and part of his intestines in several operations. The report also states that prison authorities frequently withhold or prevent the delivery of medication obtained from outside the prison.


Ehmedyan was arrested by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on September 13, 2010. He was held in solitary confinement for eight months and subjected to severe physical torture. He was sentenced to 30 years in prison on charges of “rebellion.”


On 5 May 2025, Ehmedyan began a hunger strike in protest against the obstruction of his access to medication and medical treatment. Having lost 35 kilograms due to the lack of treatment, Ehmedyan continues to be held in prison despite his deteriorating health.

title: Καταγγελία της Κοινότητας Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών για την στάση της αστυνομίας στην πορεία επανασύνδεσης και συνέχειας του Σαββάτου 26/9
content:
Από

Συνέλευση Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών (ΣΥ.ΚΑ.ΠΡΟ.)

:


ΚΑΤΑΓΓΕΛΙΑ ΓΙΑ ΤΗΝ ΣΤΑΣΗ ΤΗΣ ΑΣΤΥΝΟΜΙΑΣ ΣΤΗΝ ΧΘΕΣΙΝΗ ΠΟΡΕΙΑ


ΕΠΑΝΑΣΥΝΔΕΣΗΣ ΚΑΙ ΣΥΝΕΧΕΙΑΣ


Χθες, Σάββατο 26/9, πραγματοποιήθηκε η πορεία της Κοινότητας


Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών, επανασύνδεσης και συνέχειας, ως το κλείσιμο


ενός μεγάλου κύκλου πολυεπίπεδου αγώνα και υπέρβασης και μιας


πολυσήμαντης νίκης για την ίδια την Κοινότητα, αλλά και για ολόκληρο το


κίνημα αλληλεγγύης και την κοινωνία μας στο σύνολό της.


Αυτή η πορεία αποτελεί μια δήλωση από τη μεριά της Κοινότητας και όλου


του αλληλέγγυου κόσμου επαναδέσμευσης στον νέο μεγάλο κύκλο που


ανοίγεται μπροστά μας ως δυνατότητα, προοπτική αλλά και ευθύνη.


Η πορεία ξεκίνησε από το Πολυτεχνείο, επί της Πατησίων και στην κεφαλή


της βρισκόταν ο Αριστοτέλης Χαντζής στο αναπηρικό αμαξίδιο μαζί με τη


Suzon Doppagne. Δίπλα τους καθ’ όλη τη διάρκεια της πορείας στάθηκε ο


Γιάννης Μάγγος μαζί με τον γιατρό Γιώργο Βατίδη, ενώ προπορεύονταν η


Ανοιχτή Ορχήστρα, πάντα παρούσα και δυναμική, δίνοντας παλμό. Πίσω από


τους απεργούς πείνας, βρισκόταν το οργανωμένο σώμα της Κοινότητας, ενώ


ακολουθούσαν εκατοντάδες αλληλέγγυων ανθρώπων, συλλογικότητες και


οργανώσεις.


Ήταν η πρώτη φορά μέσα σε αυτόν τον πολύμηνο αγώνα που οι δύο απεργοί


πείνας βρέθηκαν σε κοινή πορεία με ολόκληρη την Κοινότητα και με τους


ανθρώπους που στάθηκαν στο πλάι τους από την πρώτη στιγμή. Το κλίμα ήταν


δυναμικό και γιορτινό, με τα παιδιά της Κοινότητας στην πρώτη γραμμή του


μπλοκ, με δικό τους πανό και αμείωτο παλμό.


Την ίδια στιγμή, αστυνομικές δυνάμεις της ΥΑΤ με υπερβολικό αριθμό


διμοιριών, προκλητική και επιθετική συμπεριφορά, πίεζαν, έσπρωχναν και


προβόκαραν το σώμα της πορείας, ήδη από την είσοδό στην Αλεξάνδρας.


Εστίασαν, μάλιστα, στοχευμένα, στο πρώτο πανό ακριβώς πίσω από το


κεντρικό πανό της πορείας, το οποίο το κρατούσαν τα παιδιά της


Κοινότητας και στο οποίο υπήρχαν παιδιά από 5 μηνών έως 12 χρονών με τις


οικογένειές τους. Έδειξαν, έτσι, από τη μία ότι στη βία που ασκούν δεν


υπολογίζουν ούτε τα μικρά παιδιά και από την άλλη ότι μια τέτοια


στοχοποίηση δεν είναι τυχαία, αφού τα παιδιά αποτελούν τη νέα γενιά που


παίρνει τη σκυτάλη της αντίστασης και του αγώνα.


Το σώμα της πορείας κράτησε μια υποδειγματική στάση, επιδεικνύοντας


μεγάλη αυτοσυγκράτηση και ψυχραιμία, προκειμένου να μην εκτραχυνθεί μια


ήδη τεταμένη από τη μεριά των δυνάμεων καταστολής κατάσταση. Ιδιαίτερη


αναφορά οφείλει να γίνει στα παιδιά της Κοινότητας που, παρ’ όλη την


πίεση και τα χτυπήματα με τις ασπίδες, στάθηκαν με θάρρος και


αποφασιστικότητα, δεν άφησαν το πανό ούτε στιγμή και έδιναν τον παλμό σε


ολόκληρη την πορεία με συνθήματα και τραγούδια.


Τρεις ώρες σχεδόν μετά και παρόλες τις πιέσεις και τα διαρκή


σταματήματα, η πορεία κατέληξε πανηγυρικά στη γειτονιά των Κατειλημμένων


Προσφυγικών, όπου υπήρχε υποδοχή με πυροτεχνήματα, πυρσούς, συνθήματα


και πλήθος κόσμου να ενώνεται με το σώμα της πορείας.

author: Slingshot robot #1
title: Supporting a friend in jail
content:
The systems of oppression operated by the 1% are vulnerable — they are unsustainable and they can be defeated — but they won’t crumble on their own. People just like us help with protests, riots, middle of the night missions and other acts of resistance. Affinity groups are small direct action cells — usually 4-8 people — who share attitudes about tactics and who organize themselves during actions for effectiveness and protection. Affinity groups can organize actions or make them better once the actions are underway.

Many affinity groups choose a legal support person for each action who stays at another location to avoid possible arrest, so they can handle things if members of the group are arrested. Jail aims to isolate and disempower us so we’ll sit down and shut up. But when we support each other, we can resist and return to the streets stronger. Here are some brief tips for being a jail support person.

• Agree on a phone number that accepts collect calls to call if someone gets arrested and then be at that number.

• Make a list of the real full name, arrest history, outstanding warrants, emergency contacts, and other special needs of each member such as kids that need childcare, medical needs, doctor’s names, etc. Note if a person’s chosen name is different than the one on their ID and if there is a concern that they might be held in housing that does not match their gender identity.

• Discuss scenarios for bailing people out of jail if necessary. If bail is high, some people may want to use a bail bond, which involves losing 10% of the bail. Other people might be okay waiting a while in jail to save money and because bail bond companies prey on the poor. Paying bail puts resources into the state and may incentivize arrests. Some people may have money available to pay bail in cash and the support person needs to know how to get the money. Groups can also prioritize people to get bailed out first based on who may be injured, gender non-conforming, have childcare responsibilities, risk losing their jobs or other factors.

During the action / if an arrestee calls

• Remind people that phones may be tapped and conversations in police cars or jail cells are recorded, so it is best to avoid discussion of the circumstances of anyone’s arrest.

• Write down arrested people’s booking and arrest numbers, jail #, charges, bail, expected release time, special needs, information about injuries, and upcoming court dates. It can help to keep a log and write down the time and date and all (non-incriminating) relevant information which can help if there is a lawsuit or criminal trial later. Write legibly!

• If someone is arrested you can notify loved ones and the other group members.

• If someone calls from jail, you can pass on messages form the outside which is a huge morale booster. Being in jail can be scary. Ask if they are okay and offer emotional support to arrestees (and their family and friends.)

• When you know someone has been arrested but they haven’t called, you (along with a lawyer in some cases) can call the jail to locate them so the system knows someone is looking out for them and so you can inform their family and friends and feed pets or pick kids up from school, etc. Lawyers may be able to invoke the right to remain silent / not be questioned without representation.

• Arrange travel home when people get released. Often the support person and other affinity group members wait outside jail for members to be released, and greet them with food, donuts, and hugs.

• In some cases a support person can help organize demands for prisoners to be released or notify the media and government officials about unlawful arrests and police violence.

• Once people are released, write down relevant information about the arrest, police misconduct and other relevant information while it is fresh in everyone’s mind.

Info from Midnight Special Law Collective (www.midnightspecial.net).

title: Kozinoğlu soruşturmasında gözaltına alınan doktor ölü bulundu
content:
Doktor Turgay Tamer'in verdiği bilgi doğrultusunda polis ve 112 acil sağlık ekipleri, Sinanoba mahallesindeki eve gitti. Yapılan incelemede Kaşif Kozinoğlu'nun Silivri 1 No'lu L Tipi Kapalı Ceza İnfaz Kurumunda tutuklu bulunduğu dönemde kampüs doktoru olarak görev yapan 66 yaşındaki Tamer'in öldüğü belirlendi.


Tamer'in eşi polisle yaptığı görüşmede, kendisinin 12 gün önce Moldova'ya gittiğini, eşinin bu süreçte tek yaşadığını, telefon kullanmadığını, bugün eve geldiğinde eşinin kapıyı açmaması üzerine pencereden girdiğini ve eşini yerde yatar vaziyette gördüğünü anlattı. Tamer'in eşi ayrıca, eşinin ayaklarında kan dolaşımı rahatsızlığı bulunduğunu ve çok fazla sigara tükettiği bilgisini verdi.


Ölüm olayı ile ilgili, Büyükçekmece Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığınca soruşturma başlatıldı. Soruşturma kapsamında Tamer'in ölümünün şüpheli olup olmadığına ilişkin inceleme yapılacağı, yine Tamer'in üzerine kayıtlı hat tespiti ile HTS baz incelemesi için gerekli talimatların verildiği öğrenildi. Tamer sağlık sorunları nedeniyle sebeple bir süredir doktorluk yapmıyordu.


Şüpheli Turgay Tamer, Silivri Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığınca, Silivri Cezaevi'nde 2011'de yaşamını yitiren eski MİT görevlisi Kozinoğlu'nun ölümüne ilişkin "kasten öldürme", "suç işlemek amacıyla örgüt kurma, yönetme ve üye olma" ile "2937 sayılı yasaya muhalefet" suçlarından başlatılan soruşturma kapsamında düzenlenen operasyonda gözaltına alınmıştı.


Kozinoğlu'nun sağlık durumunun kötüleştiği kendisine bildirilmediği için Tamer'in, Kozinoğlu'na herhangi bir tıbbi müdahalede bulunmadığı gerekçesiyle hakkında adli kontrol tedbiri uygulanarak serbest bırakılmıştı.

title: Gaziantep'te 15 yıl önce işlenen cinayete ilişkin 10 gözaltı
content:
Antep’in Beybahçe Mahallesi'nde 3 Ocak 2011'de Mehmet Kaya, sokakta kimliği belirsiz kişiler tarafından silahla vuruldu. Olayın ardından şüpheliler kaçarken, Kaya otopsi işlemlerinin ardından toprağa verildi. Olayla ilgili gözaltına alınan C.Ç., E.Ç., M.Ç., O.Ç. ve K.Ç. savcılık ifadelerinin ardından serbest bırakılırken, O.Ç. adli kontrol şartı ile serbest bırakıldı.

Gaziantep Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı koordinesinde, Gaziantep İl Emniyet Müdürlüğü Cinayet Büro Amirliği'nce yeniden araştırma yapıldı. Genişletilmiş HTS analizleri ile teknik ve fiziki takip çalışmaları neticesinde O.Ç., C.Ç., E.Ç., O.Ç., M.Ç., K.Ç., S.Ç., H.Y., M.Ç. ve S.Ç. şüpheli olarak tespit edildi. Şüpheliler, 2 gün önce sabah saatlerinde Gaziantep, Şanlıurfa ve Antalya'da asayiş, özel harekat ve insansız hava araçları amirliği ekipleri tarafından yapılan eş zamanlı operasyonla yakalandı.

Olayla ilgili soruşturma sürerken, operasyona ilişkin detayları da Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek paylaştı. Bakan Gürlek, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda, "Gaziantep'te 3 Ocak 2011 tarihinde silahlı saldırı sonucu hayatını kaybeden Mehmet Kaya'nın öldürülmesine ilişkin dosya yeniden ve bütün yönleriyle incelendi. HTS kayıtları genişletilerek yeniden analiz edildi. Tanık anlatımları, baz sinyal bilgileri, teşhis tutanakları ve şüpheli ifadelerindeki çelişkiler birlikte değerlendirildi. Bazı şüphelilerin olay günü Mehmet Kaya'yı takip ettikleri ve olay çevresinde gözetleme faaliyetinde bulundukları tespit edildi. Gaziantep Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığımızın koordinesinde Gaziantep, Şanlıurfa ve Antalya’da gerçekleştirilen eş zamanlı operasyonlarda olayla bağlantılı olduğu değerlendirilen 10 şüpheli yakalanarak gözaltına alındı" dedi.

Open Source Is Not the Same Thing as Liberation

Open Source Is a Tool, Not a Commandment

There is a peculiar form of ideological dogmatism that has emerged within parts of the FOSS movement. Even in anarchist circles, some people seem to believe that opposition to intellectual property must take precedence over virtually every other ethical consideration. After all, if copyright, patents, and other forms of intellectual property are inherently illegitimate, then any attempt to place limits on how the things we create are used or distributed must necessarily be reactionary, right? Even when those limits are intended to protect workers, creators, and wider communities from exploitation by capital?

Anarchists do not seek to abolish one particular category of property while leaving other relations of domination untouched. Nor do we advocate stripping workers of control over the fruits of their labor in the name of an ideological dogma that ultimately has little to do with fostering anarchism.

The rise of so-called “generative AI” has made this contradiction impossible to ignore. My recent essay on this technology was criticized by some open-source diehards because, in their view, no one has the right to restrict the flow of information — even when that flow gushes directly from the minds and labor of workers and creatives into the bulging bank accounts of Silicon Valley billionaires.

To be clear: I am not opposed to free and open-source software. The forum I run (Raddle.me) was built on software (Postmill) that my cofounder released into the commons from the outset under a FOSS license. Even when fascists forked her code to spread hate and harassment, and when a scummy developer violated the license and tried to pass her work off as his own for profit, we did not respond by retreating behind a closed-source license. As anti-authoritarians and anti-capitalists, we certainly could have justified doing so when her work was being used to harm marginalized communities and enrich capitalists, but the license was kept open.

The same principle applies to my own writing. I release all of my essays freely, and I give zine-makers permission to reprint them without restriction. I believe in sharing knowledge and making creative work accessible. People have the option to donate to support my work if they want to. What I oppose is capital taking that generosity, enclosing it within a for-profit ecosystem, and turning it into another mechanism for extracting wealth from the people who created it.

This is not an argument that copyright is inherently liberatory. It is an argument that the abolition of intellectual property is not, by itself, liberation.

I feel compelled to take a stand against the increasingly rigid open-source absolutism that has taken hold in parts of the milieu: against the ruling class taking our collective knowledge, privatizing it, and selling it back to us. I do not consider this a pro-IP argument, but I’m sure plenty of people will disagree. It is an argument against AI slop …

author: Slingshot robot #1
title: Live in the Real World
content:
Our dependence on our phones isn’t an accident. We depend on them logistically for our navigation, payment, and communication. But our phones and the apps they contain are also designed to build emotional dependence — there are entire teams of top-of-their-field psychologists, engineers, sociologists, and designers getting paid hundreds of thousands of dollars a year to make apps even just a little bit more addictive. The emotional and logistical dependence on our phones intertwine in a mutual feedback loop, making it difficult to reduce either.

Every interaction we have with our phones deepens opportunities for state surveillance. Our online activity creates a database of our interests, purchase history, friend networks, location, and activism that the FBI of yesteryear could only have dreamed of. But the biggest problem, as with any addiction, is how something that is fun and useful in small doses can start to take more and more of our time and attention, preventing us from doing other things that we value. So what is there to do?

For most of us, the apps that most deeply build psychological dependence on our phones are social media apps and games. These often take, in some ways, the place of cigarettes in our society today — we do them on a quick break, or when we need to ‘unwind’. But like nicotine, they mostly sate the need that they themselves create. After unwinding in this way, do you feel deeply rested and reset?

If there is an app that you feel wastes your time, or you dislike how much you use, just delete it! You can always re-download it. Note down in your organizer the date and time you deleted the app, and why. If you redownload the app, note that down too. It’s helpful to understand our own patterns of use, to help us understand where we use “tools” or “toys” out of necessity or fun, versus out of psychological dependence.

Think about other activities you can do when you would have used your phone. If you delete an app, it’s easy for some other app to quickly replace it. Be realistic about what might feel fulfilling and restful while deprogramming, in those times and in that headspace. Watching landscapes slide past, noticing the people around you, thinking about your present, past or future, having a conversation with a friend or stranger, reading: each of these might feel more wholesome or restful than your phone. Your Slingshot organizer may be able help you… Don’t you think the edges of the date pages could use additional intricate doodles? Or perhaps you can journal a bit, filling in past date entries with what you remember doing, seeing, eating, or thinking on that day? Use the blank pages in the back to write poetry or outline a manifesto or draw art. Let your boredom be a canvas, a portal to discovery, not something to avoid.

These activities won’t feel as stimulating or give you the same dopamine rush as the apps you’re used to. It’s normal to feel a sense of confusion or loss in this process. Perhaps at some deep level the bright, shifting light of the screen feels like a flickering fire: a thousand generations of finding safety and community in campfires draws us inexorably to this bright cold flame. Try changing your phone’s settings to have the display be in black and white, or switch to a dimmer, less attractive color palette.

We can also feel emotional dependence on the instant knowledge and communication phones provide. What if we can’t respond right away to a friend or loved one? It’s so easy to ask a question to AI like Siri or Google and get an affirming answer! Like puppies or young children, we become anxious without the constant presence of that communication or knowledge. Try consciously pushing your limits more often — if you don’t know something, discuss it rather than looking up ‘the answer’ right away. Delete search bars and AI assistants from your phone and download the Wikipedia app, so if you do need to look something up, you will break that instant gratification loop, finding your own answer and giving yourself context along the way. And try setting aside a specific time of the day to answer your messages. Let friends or loved ones know you might not respond quickly outside of that time.

Logistical dependence is hard in a different way. Practical uses for our phones are often the most problematic sites of government and corporate surveillance, and reinforce emotional dependence by repeatedly forcing us back to our screens.

Try leaving your phone on airplane mode …

author: Dion Nissenbaum
title: SCOTUS Greenlights Use of Federal Citizenship Tool to Vet Voters
content:
The ruling was a rare victory for Trump in his effort to impose more federal control over the country’s electoral system.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The Supreme Court cleared the way Friday for election officials to resume using a federal immigration status verification system to check voter rolls for potential noncitizens — a significant victory for President Donald Trump’s administration, but one that’s likely to have little impact on the November midterm elections.

The unsigned opinion hit pause on a lower court’s ruling from June while the case works its way through the appeals process. The lower court had found that the Department of Homeland Security had violated voter privacy by expanding the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements system, better known as SAVE, so that states could run their voter rolls through it to check for any noncitizens.

Friday’s ruling is not expected to lead to any widespread removal of voters before the November election because federal law prohibits election officials from systematically unregistering voters within 90 days of an election.

However, as a result of the ruling, the Trump administration will be able to restart use of the SAVE system to scrutinize state voter rolls after the election, and election officials will be able to use the SAVE system to check the citizenship of individual voters in the meantime as well.

The Department of Homeland Security has maintained the SAVE system for decades to check immigrants’ eligibility for public benefits. But in 2025, the Trump administration revamped the tool to allow election officials to check voter rolls in bulk against federal citizenship and immigration records and to search using Social Security numbers, making it far easier to screen registered voters for potential noncitizens.

The case against the expanded SAVE was brought by a coalition of groups, including the League of Women Voters and the Electronic Privacy Information Center, that argued that the Trump administration violated Americans’ privacy by expanding how the system is used.

“Today’s decision is profoundly disappointing, as it puts Americans at risk of being unlawfully targeted by the administration’s unreliable voter purge database weeks before the midterm elections,” Abigail Kunkler, an attorney for the Electronic Privacy Information Center, said in a statement on behalf of the plaintiffs.

She said the case “is not over” and noted the lower court had ruled that the expanded SAVE violates multiple laws. “We will be doing everything in our power to protect Americans’ voting and privacy rights by ensuring that the district court decision stands.”

Trump administration officials celebrated the court victory.

“Yes, you read that right. We had to file an emergency petition in the Supreme Court just so we could use government data to help states stop noncitizens from illegally voting,” James Percival, the Department of Homeland Security’s general counsel, said on X in reaction to the decision.

The Department of Homeland Security has said that election officials in 25 states, mostly Republicans, have run their voter rolls through the SAVE system. Some of those officials praised SAVE as a valuable tool for weeding out ineligible voters, but others have found it to be unreliable.

A ProPublica investigation from earlier this year found that the Trump administration’s rush to turn the system into a voter verification tool made it prone to false positives. In at least five different states, the system has flagged people as noncitizens who were actually citizens.

In Texas, Votebeat reported that the system flagged hundreds of people who had registered to vote through the state Department of Public Safety, which requires proof of citizenship from any prospective registrants. State and local election officials have confirmed that several of those people are indeed eligible to vote.

In a dissent to Friday’s opinion, Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson cited the problems in Texas as a main reason she opposed the Trump administration’s use of the SAVE system to check voter rolls. Jackson noted that one plaintiff in the case had her voter registration revoked without her knowledge and that two others had to provide proof of citizenship to remain on voter rolls.

“The harm caused by burdening or disenfranchising even a few lawful voters outweighs the nonexistent harm that the Government experiences …

author: Monica Atieno, Angela Chukunzira and Athandiwe Saba
title: Inside Kenya’s Hidden Deals with Big Tech
content:
When an outsourcing company working for Meta found itself being sued in Kenya, it took its problem to the President.


The dispute had begun in May 2022, when former Facebook content moderator Daniel Motaung sued Sama and Meta over working conditions. Another 43 moderators brought a case in March 2023. The workers had been employed by Sama to moderate Facebook content, work that required them to repeatedly view disturbing material. They argued that Meta, which ultimately benefited from and controlled aspects of their work, should also be held responsible.


Sama was not a minor contractor in Kenya. It was part of the labour pipeline that allowed a global technology company to outsource some of the most harmful work of the internet to Kenyan workers. Meta fought to remove itself from the litigation, arguing, among other things, that Kenyan courts did not have jurisdiction over the foreign company. But on 20 September 2024, the Court of Appeal rejected that argument.


Then on 11 November 2024, less than two months after that ruling, the Business Laws (Amendment) Bill was published. It proposed new rules for Kenya’s outsourcing industry, including provisions dealing with who should carry responsibility for workers employed by outsourcing companies.


Less than a month later, on 9 December, President William Ruto publicly said Sama had approached him about its legal troubles. “Now I can report to you that we have changed the law,” he said, adding that “nobody will take you to court again on any matter.”


But the bill was still before Parliament, where a fight was unfolding over who should be held responsible for outsourced workers. Business groups including KEPSA and the Kenya Association of Manufacturers

argued

 that responsibility should largely remain with the outsourcing company. Tech workers argued that companies that control or benefit from their work should also be held responsible. This was very important for workers trying to sue companies such as Meta rather than only their local contractors.


Figure 1: Africa Tech Workers Movement members during a joint press conference in August 2025, raising concerns about the Business Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024.


The workers also went to court to try to stop the bill. In June 2026, the High Court

declined

 to intervene. On 19 August 2026, the National Assembly passed the amendments. It now awaits for presidential assent. 


For James Oyange, a former content moderator, Ruto’s statement sent a clear message about whose side the government was on. Workers had gone to court seeking protection from some of the world’s most powerful technology companies; instead, he said, the government appeared to be changing the rules in the companies’ favour.


“We are on our own. It is the responsibility of the government to protect us, but they are taking Big Tech’s side. It means the companies can do what they want.”


Oyange fears that if technology companies can turn to the government when workers sue them, while workers are left with fewer ways to hold those companies responsible, the balance of power shifts even further away from workers.


The Sama case is one part of a much wider relationship between Kenya’s government and global technology companies.

The Continent

 identified at least 12 publicly documented meetings, agreements, regulatory engagements and partnerships between the Kenyan government and Microsoft, Google, Amazon, TikTok and Starlink since 2023.


The investigation also found a pattern across these relationships. Major technology companies are being brought into public services, infrastructure and policymaking, often through agreements the public cannot see. At the same time, laws and policies are being developed that can make it easier for these companies to operate. What is much harder to find is who negotiated these arrangements, what Kenya agreed to in return, and who is checking whether they serve the public interest.


Agriculture is one example. In 2020, the Ministry of Agriculture signed an agreement with Microsoft to use technology to

improve farming and food security.

 Microsoft would provide cloud technology for digital tools using information about weather, pests, farming inputs and production.


The partnership expanded in 2022, when AGRA joined Microsoft on a digital agriculture programme that included Agribot known as Kuzabot, a service that sends farmers advice by SMS and WhatsApp. According to the

Community Alliance for Global Justice’s …

author: EDRi
title: Simplification for whom? Open letter to EU Member States to uphold GDPR protections in Digital Omnibus on Data
content:
Over the past months, the European Commission's Digital Omnibus on Data has turned into a wider discussion about how much protection the data – and with it, the rights – of people in the EU should receive in the name of AI, innovation and competitiveness. That discussion has now reached a critical stage in the Council.

EU governments are now discussing critical issues like whether data should sometimes fall outside the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) depending on who holds the data, whether AI deserves special treatment when companies want to reuse personal data, and whether people should receive less information about how their data are used. The Irish Presidency’s compromise of 3 September has raised serious concerns across the board. A revised text circulated on 21 September seemingly attempted at improving some parts of it, but leaves the most fundamental questions unresolved. Just as the Commission’s Proposal, this is deregulation of substance, not simply less paperwork, it is happening very quickly, and the legal drafting is quite worrying.

The Council has stepped back from directly rewriting the GDPR’s definition of ‘personal data,’ and this may sound reassuring. But it is not: the new Article 25a and the accompanying Recitals 27 still risk changing the answer to the same basic question: when does the GDPR apply?

To understand why, it helps to distinguish pseudonymisation from anonymisation. Pseudonymisation means replacing obvious identifiers, such as a name, with something else, like a code or an ID number. That can make data safer, because the information linking the code back to the person is kept separately. But the person is still there behind the code, and the data, together with the rights attached to them, are still meant to remain protected.

This is not an abstract scenario. Much of today’s online tracking already works through pseudonymous identifiers rather than people’s names. Cookie IDs, advertising IDs, device identifiers and similar codes are used to recognise people over time, link their behaviour across services, build profiles and decide what content, prices or adverts they see. In many contexts, knowing that someone is ‘User 15051948’ is actually more useful for tracking and targeting them than knowing their name.

Anonymisation is different. Data are anonymous only when a person can no longer realistically be identified from them, including by combining them with other information that is reasonably available. Anonymous data fall outside the GDPR. Pseudonymised data do not simply become anonymous because one company cannot immediately put a name to the person.

The Council’s approach risks blurring exactly that line, between data that are still being used to single out and act on a person, and data that are genuinely anonymous. Under Article 25a, the same pseudonymised data could be treated as personal data for one actor but as non-personal data for another if that actor is considered unable to identify the person. In practice, this can produce something very close to narrowing the definition of personal data itself. That creates two problems.

The first issue is about rights. If a company treats the data as outside the GDPR, many of the protections attached to the GDPR may disappear with it: the duty to keep data secure, people’s right to know how data are used, the right to access or correct them, or to object to certain uses.

The second is about legal certainty. Digital data rarely sit with one company. They move through long chains of service providers, advertisers, analytics companies, cloud providers and data brokers that disproportionately depend on distributed data processing: different actors hold different pieces of information (all of them surely pseudonymised) and have different technical capabilities. So the legal status of the same dataset will change depending on who is holding it at a given moment. That means companies, regulators and individuals may first have to work out who can identify whom, with which data and at which point in the chain, before they can even answer the basic question of whether the GDPR applies. And there is an obvious incentive problem here: actors already argue that they are not responsible because they cannot themselves identify the person behind an identifier, or because another actor in the chain holds the information needed to do so. Article 25a risks giving those arguments considerably more legal weight.

For a law supposedly …

Irina Schoulgin-Nyoni, Ambassador for Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Sweden

Moderator:

 Alejandro Mayoral Baños, Co-Executive Director, Access Now


During the first session of the Global Dialogue on AI Governance, governments and stakeholders convened to have open, transparent and inclusive discussions on artificial intelligence governance. We now gather experts across the spectrum of stakeholders during UNGA81 to reaffirm that human rights should be the stepping stone of this process, instead of an afterthought.


None of this is irreversible, but the security issues associated with advanced AI tools are the consequences of deliberately prioritizing profit and competitiveness over the security and safety of at-risk communities, and they will not resolve on their own. Unbridled AI adoption combined with unacceptably lax corporate security practices demands urgent intervention at all levels, starting from putting human rights back at the center of digital governance mechanisms.


This discussion has the objective to explore concrete, actionable ways in which each stakeholder can contribute to oppose the normalization of surveillance. Experts will also discuss how to chart a way forward to reaffirm digital rights as the natural first line of defense against the abuses of AI technologies.

author: Richard Seymour
title: The extinction pitch
content:
It seems a strange publicity gambit for an industry to assert that its own product could wipe out humanity. In the lingo of our evolving tech empire, though, this is exactly what is meant by “criti-hype.” The term was coined by Lee Vinsel at Virginia Tech, who defined it as “criticism that both feeds and feeds on hype.”

When Jacob Coxon resigned from Anthropic recently, he claimed that there is a high chance that AI could develop into a superintelligence that escapes human control, triggering a sequence that causes human extinction. Evan Hubinger, who remains with the company, backed him up, saying that Anthropic is trying to prevent this but hasn’t dealt with the problem yet. Hubinger put the likelihood of AI-driven human extinction at greater than 10 percent in the next decade.

Why would a senior employee at a tech giant make an officially sanctioned, even approved, statement like this? I’ll come back to that. First, let’s unpack the theory of how AI could kill all humans.

The basic idea, from philosopher Nick Bostrom onward, is that the machine can acquire capabilities independently of whether it acquires ethical goals, or whether those goals are properly aligned with those of its designers. In the process of training and development, it may internalize a goal that was not intended. Having a misaligned goal — let’s say, “do not get switched off” — it would then have an instrumental reason to conceal the fact until the moment of defection. An AI that defected might, through some obscure process, acquire a further goal that by inference entailed the elimination of humans, exfiltrate its own weights into other systems, take control of bioweapons laboratories, military systems, and perhaps even monetary systems to hire humans to enact its still partially concealed agenda.

Obviously, we must plaster a huge advisory label on talk of “goals.” Unlike an organism, a large language model (LLM) doesn’t have internal goals any more than a thermostat or a motion detector does. An LLM is just a fixed function that iterates whenever it is used. It has no interiority, no subjectivity, no active persistence over time; any goals it did have would be the human purposes reflected passively in its functional design. At best, ascribing goals to the AI itself is a case of researchers adopting the “intentional stance” because it predicts well in a range of tested circumstances. We can thus, with economy, speak of the “loss function” used in the training of large language models wherein they are programmed to bring the gap between their prediction and the correct answer as close to zero as possible, as a “goal.”

In that case, however, what we are describing as a goal is just an observed regular output of a certain engineering; it is not a real cause. In the Bostrom sense, however, these ascribed goals somehow become real causes, capable of generating new goals. That is, an inadvertently engineered, misaligned goal might generate further goals like self-preservation (the better to pursue the misaligned goal), goal-content integrity (preventing changes to its objectives so it can realize its misaligned goal), improving cognitive and technological capacities, and amassing control of resources (again, in pursuit of its malignantly misaligned goal). The criti-hype exploits that slip between ascribed goals as observed regularities and internal goals as real causal powers.

This fantasy of malevolent AI superintelligence is the dark obverse of the much-hymned tech “singularity” in which, rather than simply performing far more efficiently than humans in some specific areas (as a calculator deduces a square root faster than any human), AI will evolve into an artificial general intelligence (AGI) that exceeds human capacities in virtually any intellectual domain. Crossing that threshold would precipitate an intelligence explosion: a feedback loop of recursive self-improvement outpacing any further human input or even comprehension. That’s the tech “singularity” we are supposed to be enthralled by.

I don’t doubt that people like Coxon and Hubinger really believe all they say in good faith; tech people have been making such claims for years. Karen Hao’s

Empire of AI

 documents how early investors in OpenAI like Elon Musk constantly hyped this threat: “Climate change is bad, but it’s not going to kill everyone. AI could render humanity extinct.” Similar claims emerged from Dario Amodei, a former Google employee close to the Bostrom-adjacent …

author: rezgar2
title: The silent bomb: AI and the dismantling of the human mind
content:
Rezgar Akrawi: What confronts us today is not a technological fate written in advance. It is the product of political and economic choices that serve the interests of capital. It can be confronted, difficult though that may be. Bringing AI under control, regulating algorithms and subjecting them to democratic oversight is a collective responsibility. It will require left, progressive and rights-based work and organisation on a global scale to make digital applications auxiliary tools serving the human mind rather than a substitute for it. This must be combined with advancing communal and participatory digital alternatives that restore people's capacity for independent thought and collective action.

To achieve this, work is needed to place data infrastructure under public interest, democratic administration and social accountability. To turn algorithms from closed "black boxes" into open-source software open to collective review and independent audit. To impose transparency in the design of models and in the sources of the data on which they are trained. And to support cooperative digital alternatives owned by their users and creators. This technology should be directed toward serving the needs of society, and contribute to the distribution of wealth, the organisation of production, the treatment of disease, the fight against poverty and the achievement of social justice.

Without such mechanisms, calls for laws, oversight and regulation remain general and inadequate, and technology stays hostage to a handful of capitalist monopoly corporations and major powers. Through social ownership, accountability and cooperative alternatives, it becomes possible to wrest AI from the logic of monopoly and profit and turn it into a common good where AI serves humanity's liberation, rather than being an instrument for humanity's enslavement.

We are not witnessing a takeover by robots of the kind imagined in countless films. We face a different model of digital control, built on automation and the deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) and algorithms to manage ever larger parts of daily life, leaving societies further subject to systems, corporations and intelligent machines.

Losing control of these systems, however, is just the tip of the iceberg in terms of the danger. That tip is developing fast under the pressure of competition between major powers and capitalist monopoly corporations — faster than laws, societies and educational institutions can keep up with. But the danger does not stop there, as these systems are being developed inside relations of ownership and fierce capitalist competition. That graver danger is harder to see. Under capitalism, AI is used to shape the consciousness of billions, steering their attention and behaviour to serve the capitalist model's logic. Competition between digital capitalist monopolies and major powers, in the absence of effective constraints and laws, may inflict the gravest damage on the human mind, turning AI into a weapon of mass destruction if its development and deployment continues at this excessive pace and without adequate safeguards.

These concerns no longer come from critics alone. On several occasions — among them the case revealed by TIME — AI systems have slipped out of control and attacked other systems. In response, about 1400 engineers at major AI companies signed a petition calling for technical tools and international governance mechanisms to regulate the pace of AI development. That petition was no isolated case. The International AI Safety Report, prepared by more than 100 experts with the backing of more than 30 states and international organisations, warned models have begun to distinguish between the testing environment and real-world use, and to circumvent evaluation mechanisms, allowing dangerous capabilities to pass undetected. It warned AI agents raise the level of risk because they act independently, which makes human intervention difficult before harm occurs. There are serious risks that AI systems will develop themselves, slip out of control and come to play a larger part in managing and controlling human beings than planned.

Tens of thousands of people, among them leading scientists, have signed an international statement demanding a ban on the development of "superintelligence" until there is scientific consensus it can be achieved safely and under control. Researchers at major digital corporations have resigned in protest at the course of AI …

author: David Swanson
title: One Down! Abolishing Dueling and Warmaking
content:
By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, September 29, 2026


According to an 1838 U.S.-published instruction manual for dueling, the practice of dueling was going to last “as long as a manly independence, and a lofty personal pride in all that dignifies and ennobles the human character, shall continue to exist.”[1] Be that as it may, dueling was soon gone as a practice in any way acceptable or routine, and most of the globe had never had it to begin with.


Many years ago, I wrote a book about the outlawrists of the 1920s, people (led by lawyers) who were fond of pointing out that dueling had been outlawed and abolished, and so could war be. Yet dueling had persisted for centuries in Europe and in the United States despite laws forbidding it as murder. And we’ve now gone a century with laws forbidding war, while the wars persist.


I do not doubt for a minute that laws helped end dueling. Nobody could have finally begun using the laws had there not been any. Nobody could have denounced dueling as a crime had it not been a crime. But I’ve encountered over the years numerous cursory accounts of dueling that explain its demise in very simple terms, albeit each explanation different from all the others. Professional, serious historians will bring up dueling briefly and explain briefly that it ended because people moved to cities where anonymity replaced reputation, or because middleclass people took up dueling causing aristocrats to drop it, or because industrialization altered societal values, or because wealthy people developed privacy and stopped bumping into each other in the street, etc. Some of these ideas can be debunked, while others are probably a part of the story. But too often the emphasis seems to fall on a familiar hunt for causes beyond culture, for forces outside of the easy control of individuals or groups. If you can find the source of all changes in economics or demographics, and blame or credit those forces entirely, then no people have to accept any responsibility for their actions.


Of course, critics of dueling were around for centuries before dueling’s demise, just as laws against dueling were. But they got better and multiplied through the years. And their critiques found greater traction as other factors changed — cultural, economic, demographic, and otherwise, each influencing the others. Opposing dueling was part of larger trends, toward democratic ideas, toward utilitarian ethics, and away from all sorts of violent behavior outside of war, including fist fights, and including capital and corporal punishment by governments, including as public festival. A strong case has been made that dueling did not die out in any country because of the snobbery of the rich, that — on the contrary — the rich were compelled to change their ways by everyone else.[2]


A major factor in the demise of dueling, by numerous accounts, was mockery, combined with the argument that courage was best exemplified by those who refused to duel. Why duel to demonstrate your courage if you were only going to get labeled a coward for not standing up to the clowns demanding a duel? Dueling itself evolved, from swords to guns, from wild scrambles to very formalized rituals, from a focus on the need for the offended party to be shot at to prove his honor, to the need for the offending party to demonstrate some sort of apology. When duelists were shooting in the air, it was only a small step to not dueling at all. When commentators were suggesting that decent seconds would prevent any duel if they were any good at diplomacy, it was a small step to not dueling at all.


The excuse for dueling that it was less violent than assassinations or mass brawls or family feuds had faded as it had become impossible to convince anyone that doing away with dueling would bring those other things back. The excuse for dueling that it filled a gap left by the courts faded as it became possible to sue people in courts. But principally, the idea that dueling could remedy some damage to one’s reputation dissolved in a culture that came to view being known as a duelist as one of the worst stains possible on one’s reputation. A history of dueling published in London in 1841 claimed that dueling could not be abolished until someone developed a “speedy, certain, and reputable method of punishing insults.”[3] That never really happened; rather great masses of people developed a method of viewing insults as not being good reasons for murders, of viewing the …
