title: Gülbeyaz: Lasting peace requires the state to embrace diversity
content:
Abdurrahman Gülbeyaz said trust cannot be rebuilt through political rhetoric alone and that democracy requires the state to adapt to society’s diversity, rather than the other way around.


Professor Abdurrahman Gülbeyaz of Nagasaki University spoke to ANF about the Peace and Democratic Society Process, examining it not merely in terms of ending the conflict and removing weapons from the equation, but also as a process of rebuilding society's political, social and cultural relationships.


Gülbeyaz discussed the conditions necessary for a democratic society, the social and political foundations of lasting peace, the need to redefine relations between the state and society, and the resolution of the Kurdish question. He emphasised the importance of building a shared life while preserving differences.


Democracy means the state adapting to society


Is it enough to understand the concept of a democratic society solely in terms of political rights? What are its social and cultural requirements?


I would like to begin with a minor objection to the premise of this question. The moment we reduce a democratic society to a catalogue of political rights, we risk inadvertently turning society once again into an object on the state's table of legal and administrative classifications. Political rights are, of course, indispensable. Without freedom of expression and association, the right to vote and stand for election, and equality before the law, democracy cannot even be contemplated. But we must remember that these rights do not, in themselves, constitute a democratic society. They are the minimum formal prerequisites that make it possible to conceive of and undertake the construction of such a society.


I have pointed out on other occasions that it is misleading to regard society and the state as two entities belonging to the same category. Society is, by its very nature, an open and dynamic system, almost organic in character. It responds to external influences and impulses, changing and transforming through its interaction with them. The state, by contrast, seeks to stabilise existing conditions, make them permanent and predictable, classify them and thereby keep them as controllable as possible.


Democracy, in this sense, does not mean that the state should impose its own mould on society through more lenient or compassionate methods. Rather, it means that the state must learn, at an institutional level, to accommodate society's changing nature, plurality and unpredictability, and transform itself accordingly. In other words, democracy is not about the state making society resemble itself. Quite the opposite: it is about the state adapting itself to society and accommodating society's concrete realities.


Language emerges here as the most crucial and decisive factor. It is clearly impossible to conceive of human beings or society independently of language. Language is the chemistry of socialisation. It is the fundamental medium that connects individuals and makes a shared social space possible.


Consequently, if the state controls, restricts and regulates the use of a language within a historically established society, democracy cannot meaningfully be said to exist in that country. If, for example, a language is permitted in the home but excluded from education, public administration, local services and the institutions that confer social prestige, even placing ballot boxes on every street corner would not make that society democratic.


The issue is not simply integrating Kurds into the existing system


Turning to Turkey, reducing the resolution of the Kurdish question to the recognition of certain political rights for Kurds is not merely inadequate; it is fundamentally wrong. The issue is not about enabling Kurds to integrate more easily into the existing system, but about transforming that system so that it can accommodate a pluralistic social reality.


The material foundations of a democratic society require the state to transform itself in ways that make multilingual education and public administration possible, allow elected local authorities to exercise genuine decision-making power and initiative, and enable different collective memories to coexist in the public sphere without suppressing one another.


There is also what I call the “minority principle”. Social emancipation does not begin with the majority generously making room for minorities. A transformation is genuinely emancipatory only to the extent …

title: Court orders release of comedian Deniz Göktaş after sentences of 19 months and 5 days
content:
The first hearing in the trial of detained comedian Deniz Göktaş, who faced allegations of “insulting the president,” “inciting the public to hatred and hostility,” and “praising crime and criminals,” was held at the Istanbul 14th Criminal Court of First Instance.


In his defense, Göktaş said the charges against him were based on four sentences he had used in his show Dead Sea. He stated that he had delivered these lines hundreds of times in different cities across Turkey and that audience reactions to the performances had consisted solely of laughter and applause.


Göktaş argued that criminalizing political humor and criticism could lead to self-censorship. He rejected the charges and requested acquittal.


‘I have been in a cell for 88 days’


Göktaş also drew attention to the length of his detention, telling the panel of judges: “I’ve been in a cell for 88 days. Of course, I’m going to speak.”


In his defense, Göktaş said that describing the president as a “shy dictator” was a political characterization and stated that he would continue expressing his criticism through humor.


He also referred to complaints filed against him through CIMER, Turkey’s presidential communications center. Göktaş said that a total of 185 complaints had been included in the case file and that they were the result of an organized campaign.


During the hearing, the prosecutor presented the final opinion, requesting that Göktaş be convicted of the charges and released.


In its ruling, the court acquitted Göktaş of the charge of “praising crime and criminals.” The charge, initially considered as “inciting the public to hatred and hostility or insulting the public,” was instead classified as “insulting religious values,” for which Göktaş received a prison sentence of 7 months and 15 days.


Göktaş was also sentenced to 11 months and 20 days in prison for “insulting the president.”


Following its ruling, the court ordered Deniz Göktaş’s release.

title: Shengal Mountain is the guarantee of life
content:
Shengal Mountain is not merely a place of refuge, but the only guarantee of survival for Yazidis. As the withdrawal of the International Coalition approaches and the risk of a potential security vacuum grows, attempts at disarmament and threats against those defending the mountain are fuelling fears of a repeat of the 2014 scenario. This comes despite the fact that the people of Shengal have received no meaningful support from the state beyond empty promises. For Yazidis, the defence forces on Shengal Mountain are not merely an armed force. They are the last stronghold of their existence and their only guarantee after they were abandoned by all forces and states during one of the darkest periods in their history. On the map, Shengal Mountain is not simply a military zone. It is the only path to survival, a mother who embraced her children when everyone else left them to die.


No one remained when all regular and irregular forces withdrew from Shengal. At that moment, tens of thousands of Yazidis had no option other than the mountain, which protected them from abduction and death. The people of the mountain armed themselves with the limited means available to them and fought to stop the attacks by ISIS mercenaries. For this reason, any suggestion that the mountain should be taken out of the hands of its people amounts to depriving the victims of their last refuge. Today, we are hearing the same old approach expressed in new terms: “establishing control, restricting weapons under state authority and ending the presence of armed forces on the mountain.” But what kind of control are they talking about, and whom do they intend to exclude? Yazidis who took up arms to defend their dignity and their land after the genocide are being portrayed as a “threat”, while dozens of armed groups operating across the country continue their activities without restriction.


The government’s position has changed. Promises to integrate Shengal fighters into the security system and recognise their rights have given way to threats and rhetoric about taking control of the mountain. This shift has prompted considerable speculation. Concerns have been heightened further by reports of a new agreement reminiscent of the 2014 deal. At the time, cooperation over Shengal was reportedly arranged in exchange for Kirkuk. A similar scenario is now being discussed: negotiations over the Yazidi region, the handover of Shengal Mountain in exchange for Turkey’s withdrawal from its base in Zilkan (Bashiqa), all coinciding with the withdrawal of the International Coalition.


The threat is approaching


The threat is approaching, and 1 October is a date that everyone should be watching closely. Official statements identify 30 September as the deadline for ending the International Coalition’s military mission and completing the withdrawal of its forces, with 1 October expected to mark the beginning of a new period in which the country is free of any foreign military presence. This withdrawal creates a genuine security vacuum, and experience has shown that minorities and women are the first to pay the price. The events of 2014 are not a distant memory. If violence erupts, developments could unfold suddenly and rapidly. Could today’s rhetoric about taking control of the mountain be intended to pave the way for renewed attacks of the kind seen in 2014, when ISIS mercenaries were prevented from advancing onto the mountain? These questions remain unanswered.


What has the government done for Shengal until now, and why is it threatening those who defend it today? Was it the government, rather than the defence forces on the mountain, that saved the people of Shengal? Did it open the mass graves and establish the fate of the missing? Did it prevent women from being sold in markets? Did it rebuild the devastated Shengal? Did it compensate the people? Or did it resolve the displacement crisis and bring displaced people home from the camps? We have seen nothing but empty promises. What we see today is nothing but threats. Shengal Mountain is neither a bargaining chip nor something to be traded. Those who genuinely want to protect Iraq and build the state should begin by disarming militias that threaten the state and its institutions and undermine social peace, rather than disarming victims who defend their own mountain to prevent another genocide. Protecting the mountain means protecting the dignity of the state itself, because it means protecting a people whom the …

title: Süleyman Çarnewa: Art’s role in peace is as vital as politics
content:
Koma Amed, one of the signatories of the “1,001 Signatures for a Democratic Republic and Peace” campaign, spoke to ANF about the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Speaking on behalf of the group, Süleyman Çarnewa stressed the importance of art and artists on the path to peace. 


Leaving behind the crowds of Beyoğlu and walking for a while through its narrow side streets, we came across the familiar sign. The moment we stepped into the institution that has nurtured countless artists since 1991, we were greeted warmly with broad smiles.


 


Koma Amed, which made a major impact in the 1990s, is continuing rehearsals at the Mesopotamia Cultural Centre ahead of its concert tomorrow, 30 September, at the Harbiye Open-Air Theatre.


Last year, the group was enthusiastically welcomed in Diyarbakır (Amed) after 30 years, but the same enthusiasm in Istanbul was cut short when the Governor’s Office banned its concert. The group also announced that it had cancelled its Ankara concert because of attacks on Rojava. Koma Amed eventually ended its 30-year absence from the Istanbul stage by lighting the Newroz fire in Yenikapı.


Koma Amed was also among the first signatories of the “1,001 Signatures for a Democratic Republic and Peace” campaign, launched on 12 September.


We signed the campaign because we need peace


Koma Amed, preparing to take the stage in Istanbul once again, answered our agency’s questions before rehearsals. Speaking on behalf of the group, Süleyman Çarnewa stressed the importance of art and artists on the path to peace.


Süleyman Çarnewa said they had signed the “1,001 Signatures for a Democratic Republic and Peace” campaign, which brought together figures from different sections of society, on its first day. He said, “We joined the campaign immediately, from the very first day, because we believe that every intellectual, every artist and every socially conscious person should sign it.”


The singer explained why they had signed the campaign: “Times of war, times without democracy and peace, are when the voices of art, artists and intellectuals are silenced the most. It is our voices, the voices of artists and intellectuals, that are suppressed most of all. We need peace. That is why, of course, we signed this campaign immediately.”


Süleyman Çarnewa also discussed how the pressure on the Kurdish language, spoken across Turkey, had affected art. He said: “People always say that music has no language. Yet Kurdish music has been one of the least heard voices in this region, even though nearly half of the people in this country, in this geography, speak this language. That is why we sometimes think, ‘We have to bring this language and this music to people who have never encountered them before. To the Black Sea, the Aegean, Marmara, across the entire country…’


There is no rule in life that says Kurdish music is only for Kurds, Turkish music only for Turks or English music only for the English. As Koma Amed, and later through Koma Çarnewa, which we formed as members of Koma Amed, we took these songs, the songs and stories of this land, to more than half the world.


Yet there was one thing we could never explain to anyone: that this music is not sufficiently free in the very land where we ourselves live, where we were born and raised. It is very difficult to explain because people ask, ‘How can that be? How can the voice of music, the voice of art, or art and music themselves harm people? How can they be dangerous?’”


As Koma Amed, we want to play our part in the peace process


Çarnewa stressed the importance of art on the path to peace and said: “What we need now is peace. As Koma Amed, we want to take responsibility in this peace process. We want to play our part. Why? We are standing here in front of the sign of the Mesopotamia Cultural Centre. In the 1990s, we spent years working and struggling in this cultural centre, striving to pass Kurdish culture on to future generations. We are among those who have felt the pain most deeply. That is why we believe the role of music and art is at least as essential as the role of politics.”


Çarnewa also discussed Abdullah Öcalan’s Call for Peace and Democratic Society on 27 February 2025 and said: “Mr. Öcalan’s call for peace to be built in this region, as well as the struggle he has waged for this over the years, is extremely valuable. It is also very important for freeing this region from bloodshed, war and poverty. I believe Mr. Abdullah Öcalan’s …

author: CNT Aragón-Rioja
title: 3 de octubre. La CNT Aragón-Rioja conmemora en Caspe el 90 aniversario del Consejo Regional de Defensa de Aragón
content:
Una jornada para recordar cuando 500.000 aragoneses/as se organizaron sin Estado,  y para demostrar que aquel mundo nuevo sigue siendo posible.


Hace casi un siglo, el pueblo de Aragón demostró que otra forma de organizarse y de vivir era posible. Este

sábado 3 de octubre, en Caspe

, recogemos ese legado revolucionario con una jornada conmemorativa por el

90 aniversario del Consejo Regional de Defensa de Aragón

. Habrá exposición, charla con la historiadora Assumpta Castillo, documental, homenaje, cancionero libertario y comida fraternal.


Programa: sábado 3 de octubre en Caspe


10:30 h · Apertura e inauguración de la exposición.

 Muestra documental y material histórico sobre las colectividades de Aragón. Ayuntamiento de Caspe (Plaza España, 1).


11:30 h · Charla y debate «El Consejo de Aragón y la guerra»

, a cargo de Assumpta Castillo Cañiz, doctora en Historia por la Universidad de Lleida. Ayuntamiento de Caspe (Plaza España, 1).


14:00 h · Comida fraternal.

 Comida conjunta previa reserva mediante formulario

https://cloud.cnt.es/apps/forms/s/mczWXzJkxk5aStSdoCfqQe4p


16:00 h · Proyección y coloquio del documental «Sueños colectivos».

 Ayuntamiento de Caspe (Plaza España, 1).


18:00 h · Homenaje al Consejo de Aragón.

 Plaza de España, 2, Casa Palacio Piazuelo Barberán.


18:30 h · Cancionero libertario y clausura.

 Plaza de España, 2, Casa Palacio Piazuelo Barberán.


Apúntate a la comida


Para reservar tu plaza en la comida entra en este enlace:

https://cloud.cnt.es/apps/forms/s/mczWXzJkxk5aStSdoCfqQe4p


Te pedimos que reserves cuanto antes para que podamos organizarlo bien

.


Anímate a venir, trae a tus familiares y amistades, y difunde la convocatoria entre tus contactos.


¡Nos vemos en Caspe!


Salud y anarcosindicalismo,


¿Qué fue el Consejo de Aragón?


Tras el golpe militar de julio de 1936, las tres capitales aragonesas cayeron en manos de los fascistas y en la mitad oriental de Aragón se hundieron las estructuras del Estado. Ese vacío de poder lo ocupó el pueblo. Se formaron comités revolucionarios en los pueblos y el campesinado aragonés, con una fuerte implantación de la CNT, se organizó en colectividades.


El 6 de octubre de 1936, en un Pleno Extraordinario celebrado en Bujaraloz, 174 delegados de los sindicatos de 139 pueblos acordaron crear el Consejo Regional de Defensa de Aragón (CRDA). Presidido por el anarcosindicalista Joaquín Ascaso, el Consejo pasó a coordinar unas 450 colectividades rurales, en un territorio de unos 25.000 km² y en torno a medio millón de habitantes. Se organizó desde abajo, con federaciones, consejos y colectividades. Durante 1936-1937, Aragón fue la capital internacional del anarquismo, con Caspe como capital. Una experiencia revolucionaria casi única en la historia.


El Consejo demostró en la práctica que la autogestión a gran escala y la economía libertaria eran viables, un hito que trascendió la teoría utópica clásica.


El CRDA fue un logro de la CNT, una institución que nació de la organización de los/as trabajadores. Por eso recordarlo no es solo un ejercicio de nostalgia. Hoy, la CNT continua la lucha, practicando el apoyo mutuo entre trabajadores y construyendo autogestión y sindicalismo en los centros de trabajo. Esta jornada es una forma de recoger su testigo y de reafirmar que ese mundo nuevo fue y sigue siendo posible.

title: I Si Tav scendono in piazza: una vittoria No Tav
content:
Doveva essere la risposta del fronte Sì Tav. La dimostrazione che, nonostante anni di cantieri, proteste e contestazioni, attorno alla Torino-Lione esistesse un consenso ampio e capace di mobilitarsi. Eppure ieri a Torino, si sono presentate forse 200 persone, pure secondo la Digos. Boni, probabilmente rimandato più volte in matematica nella sua carriera scolastica, ne conta 700: ma anche se fosse, il risultato non cambia.


Da No Tav Info


Non è servito lo slogan: «No alla violenza, sì alla Tav» che voleva legare il sostegno all’opera alla condanna della “violenza dei No Tav” e presentarsi come risposta politica in netta contrapposizione a chi si oppone alla Torino-Lione. L’esito, però, è difficile da trasformare nella prova di forza che evidentemente si cercava.


Anche la fotografia della politica istituzionale è triste. Il Pd non c’è, così come il sindaco Stefano Lo Russo. Non c’è Calenda. Ci sono Alberto Cirio (che ci aspettavamo si sarebbe presentato con pìc e pala), Maurizio Marrone – che non ha perso di fare polemica da campagna elettorale come è solito fare il suo partito – e i soliti rappresentanti delle forze che hanno aderito al presidio che da anni utilizzano la stessa retorica trita e ritrita su progresso e legalità (anche se il più pulito c’ha la rogna).


Raccontano che la Torino-Lione sarebbe sostenuta da un consenso ampio, trasversale, scontato. Che il dissenso sarebbe soltanto il rumore di una minoranza, mentre il territorio e la società avrebbero ormai scelto da che parte stare.


Avevano un’occasione ghiotta per dimostrarlo. Eppure…anche chi si dice Sì Tav evidentemente si sono vergognati di partecipare (a parte chi ha la faccia di tola, per dirlo garbatamente). La credibilità evidentemente non è di casa.


Quando non supportati da dichiarazioni o comunicati diffusi enormemente a mezzo stampa, ecco che le carte in tavola vengono svelate. Bastava una piazza a chiarirlo.


Siamo molto inteneriti dalla narrazione di questo grande flop, su cui davvero neanche ci sentiamo di infierire troppo data la sua insignificanza. È questo il dato da evidenziare. Non il numero di persone ma che

il presidio di ieri non fosse per nulla incisivo. Sicuramente servito per fare un bel bagno di realtà, anche se, così come l’ormai obsolescenza dell’opera, non lo ammetteranno mai.


L’intento della giornata era dimostrare di essere forti, coesi e presenti in grande numero sul territorio. Di essere la maggioranza schiacciante che dimostra l’utilità e la realizzabilità dell’opera.


Purtroppo, cari Sì Tav, la piazza ha raccontato proprio un’altra cosa.


Non vorremmo metterci sulla competizione numerica e qualitativa – ma forse anche sì – però ci piace pensare ai bei volti sorridenti delle 20mila persone di quel giorno, giovani e diversamente giovani insieme, che dopo più di trent’anni di opposizione all’opera, hanno partecipato alla Marcia del 25 luglio che tanto vi premeva stigmatizzare.


Valutate voi dove sta il futuro.


Noi intanto

ci prepariamo alla bellissima Marcia Popolare che ci sarà sabato da Sant’Ambrogio ad Avigliana, a trent’un anni di distanza dalla prima manifestazione No Tav del 1995, che proprio era partita dallo stesso paese.

author: cnt.es
title: La CIT celebra su III Congreso y renueva su Secretaría General
content:
La Confederación Internacional del Trabajo (CIT) ha celebrado su III Congreso el pasado fin de semana en Italia, un encuentro en el que las organizaciones que forman parte de la Internacional han abordado la situación de sus secciones y han renovado parte de sus responsabilidades internas.


Uno de los principales cambios acordados durante el Congreso ha sido la renovación de la Secretaría General de la CIT. El compañero Jakub ha asumido la Secretaría General, tomando el relevo de la anterior secretaria, que ha culminado su mandato. El cambio supone una nueva etapa en la coordinación de la organización internacional y de las distintas secciones que la integran.


El Congreso también ha servido para dar la bienvenida a dos nuevas secciones de la Internacional: la FGWM de Myanmar y la FOB de Brasil. Ambas organizaciones han participado en el Congreso y han quedado incorporadas a los trabajos de la CIT. La incorporación de nuevas secciones refuerza la presencia internacional de la organización y permite ampliar los vínculos entre organizaciones anarcosindicalistas y sindicalistas revolucionarias de distintos territorios.


La participación de la sección de Myanmar tuvo además una especial relevancia por las dificultades a las que se enfrenta la organización en su territorio. Durante el encuentro se explicó la situación de sus militantes y las circunstancias en las que desarrollan su actividad sindical, incluyendo la presión y vigilancia policial que sufren. La participación en el Congreso permitió poner en común esta realidad con el resto de organizaciones de la Internacional.


Durante el Congreso también se ratificó la participación de otras secciones, entre ellas la sección francesa, CNTF, y la sección británica, IWW Wisera, además de otras organizaciones vinculadas a la Internacional. Estos encuentros permitieron compartir información sobre las diferentes realidades sindicales y sociales y avanzar en la coordinación internacional.


La dimensión internacional constituye uno de los elementos centrales de la CIT. El intercambio de experiencias entre organizaciones de diferentes países permite conocer de primera mano las dificultades que afrontan las trabajadoras y trabajadores en cada territorio y establecer mecanismos de solidaridad y apoyo mutuo.


El Congreso ha servido, por tanto, no solo para abordar cuestiones organizativas internas, sino también para fortalecer los vínculos entre las diferentes secciones de la CIT y continuar construyendo una organización internacional basada en la solidaridad, la acción sindical y la coordinación entre organizaciones.


Desde las diferentes secciones se continuará trabajando para consolidar estos vínculos y afrontar conjuntamente los retos que plantea la situación internacional de la clase trabajadora.


La entrada

La CIT celebra su III Congreso y renueva su Secretaría General

 se publicó primero en

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: Unknown
title: Ritorno al nucleare in Italia
content:
Mercoledì 23 settembre il Senato ha approvato il

disegno di legge sul nucleare

 presentato dal Consiglio dei ministri all’inizio del 2025, dopo il via libera della Camera a inizio giugno.


Da Radio Blackout


Si tratta di una

legge delega

: un provvedimento con cui il

parlamento attribuisce al governo la facoltà di legiferare

 su una materia attraverso uno o più decreti legislativi,

da scrivere nei prossimi 24 mesi

. Il punto più complesso e preoccupante è che il testo si muove in nome della “

neutralità tecnologica

“: saranno i decreti attuativi a stabilire quali soluzioni potranno essere utilizzate, sulla base di “maturità, sicurezza e sostenibilità”.


Quello che si sa è che il DDL esclude le grandi centrali tradizionali e limita le installazioni agli

SMR (Small Modular Reactors)

, una tecnologia ancora in fase di sviluppo, ma

propagandata come già esistente

. In realtà non ce ne sono di operativi perché

non sono economicamente convenienti a livello di produzione

: sono piccoli e producono poca energia (100-150 MW), in Italia ne servirebbero tra i 40-80 per coprire la percentuale di fabbisogno invocata dal governo. Decine di comunità si troverebbero quindi un reattore vicino a casa, senza tutele

sulla sicurezza delle centrali e sulla gestione delle scorie, punti non affrontati all’interno del DDL

.


È evidente la natura ideologica dello slancio verso l’energia nucleare

. Invece di investire sulle rinnovabili, si presenta la fissione nucleare come una

tecnologia matura, green

 ma soprattutto come una soluzione ponte, mentre si continua a inseguire l’idea della fusione. Il piano poggia su una visione irrealistica dei tempi di sviluppo di queste tecnologie, comunque troppo lunghi rispetto all’urgenza di decarbonizzare e di mitigare il cambiamento climatico. Nel ddl, inoltre, manca qualsiasi riferimento alle

risorse consumate dalle centrali

, in particolare all’acqua, che andrebbe presa in considerazione visto l’aggravarsi delle siccità legate al cambiamento climatico. Non si affronta nemmeno il tema dello

smaltimento e del trasporto delle scorie

, che diventerebbe cruciale con impianti dislocati in tanti territori.


Da un lato si insegue quindi l’obiettivo dell’indipendenza energetica, in un contesto di difficoltà di approvvigionamento dei combustibili fossili; dall’altro, vista la

natura intrinsecamente dual-use della tecnologia nucleare

, la vicenda va letta nel

contesto generale del riarmo europeo

.


In questo senso sono emblematici

progetti come lo statunitense PELE

, che punta a realizzare piccoli reattori trasportabili su gomma per produrre energia elettrica e

alimentare basi militari in teatri e territori “ostili”

, o ANPI per la produzione di nuove armi alimentate da SMR. Anche l’Italia va in questa direzione, puntando alla nuclearizzare della marina militare (progetto MINERVA) e con la

joint venture Nuclitalia

, di cui fa parte Leonardo, che avrà quindi libero accesso alla tecnologia SMR una volta sviluppata per supposti scopi civili.


Ne abbiamo parlato con

Alessandro Ferretti, docente di Fisica all’Università di Torino

 e autore del blog

https://alessandroferrettiblog.wordpress.com/

author: Unknown
title: Ephéméride des luttes : 28 septembre
content:
Ce 28 septembre marque un jalon important de l'éphéméride des luttes : la constitution de la première internationale, qui engendrera plus ou moins logiquement et capillairement toutes les actions qui s'ensuivent.


1864 :

 A Londres, vers St. Martin's Hall, congrès constitutif de la Première Internationale.


1879 :

 A Marseille, naissance au 29 rue Navarin d'Alexandre Marius Jacob, cambrioleur anarchiste bien connu.


1883 :

 A Rüdesheim-sur-le-Rhin en Allemagne, attentat manqué des anarchistes Emil Küchler, Franz Reinhold Rupsch et August Reinsdorf contre l'empereur Guillaume et les princes qui inauguraient un monument à la gloire des armées allemandes.


1943 :

 - Au Danemark, les militant-e-s anti-nazis dans la clandestinité organisent le passage de la population juive vers la Suède.


 A Naples, c'est la deuxième journée de l'insurrection de Naples, qui au bout de 4 jours en fera la première grande ville à se libérer de l'occupant nazi, sans l'aide des Alliés.


1958 :

 En France, une nouvelle constitution est approuvée : c'est la naissance de la cinquième République.


1973 :

 Aux USA, le Weather Underground fait sauter la branche Amérique Latine de l'entreprise ITT pour son rôle dans le coup d'état au Chili

17 jours plus tôt

.


1975 :

 A Caterham en Angleterre, une bombe de l'IRA explose, faisant quelques dégâts matériels.


1977 :

 - A Madrid, les GRAPO (Groupes de résistance antifasciste du premier octobre) abattent un capitaine de police.


 A Florence, des membres des Comités Communistes de Combat incendient trois agences immobilières qui spéculent en laissant des appartements vides pour faire monter les loyers à des prix exorbitants pour les pauvres.


1978 :

 - A Rome, un militant sympathisant communiste, Ivo Zini, est assassiné par un groupe néofasciste clandestin, les NAR.


 A Turin, les Brigades Rouges tirent dans les jambes du directeur de l'usine Lancia de Chivasso. Si l'intention n'était que de le blesser aux jambes, celui-ci mourra quelques heures plus tard de ses blessures.


1998 :

 A Londres, premier festival Queeruption, qui ramène des centaines d'anarcho-queers dans la ville.


1999 :

 A Plévin en Bretagne, un commando de huit militants d'ETA cambriole l'entreprise Titanite et repart avec plus de huit tonnes de dynamite et 6000 détonateurs.


2000 :

 A Jérusalem, la visite d'Ariel Sharon marque le début de la Seconde Intifada.


2014 :

 A Hong Kong, dans le cadre du mouvement Occupy, des milliers de personnes occupent les quartiers généraux du gouvernement. La police charge et fait usage de lacrymogènes mais énormément de gens restent sur place.


Voir aussi

l'éphéméride anarchiste

 du 28 septembre.

author: Natalia Viana
title: Família de condenado por garimpo na terra Yanomami bancou vida de Ramagem nos EUA
content:
“Oii Pri, boa noite. Você tem como me enviar uma conta do apartamento de vocês no nome do meu pai? Água, luz, telefone, internet… Vamos tentar tirar a driver license do Alexandre amanhã no DMV”, diz a primeira mensagem. E a seguir: “Fiz o contrato aqui também para ele levar como se tivesse alugado o quarto. Vamos ver como vai ser”.


Essas mensagens de WhatsApp fazem parte da investigação da Polícia Federal (PF) sobre a fuga de Alexandre Ramagem para os Estados Unidos em setembro do ano passado. Elas foram enviadas por Celso Rodrigo de Mello, filho de Rodrigo Martins de Mello, conhecido como Rodrigo Cataratas, para a esposa de seu pai em 15 de setembro de 2025. Cataratas foi condenado em fevereiro deste ano a mais de 16 anos de prisão por liderar uma organização criminosa responsável pela mineração ilegal de cassiterita e ouro dentro da Terra Indígena Yanomami. Em resposta, Priscila Freitas de Melo diz apenas “Oi

 Deixa eu ver aqui”. DMV é o departamento estadual de trânsito da Flórida.


As mensagens fazem parte de uma série de diálogos, fotos e notas recuperados do celular de Priscila aos quais a

Agência Pública

 teve acesso.

Elas comprovam que a família de Rodrigo Cataratas ciceroneou, forneceu auxílio material e hospedou Ramagem logo na sua chegada à Flórida, foragido do Brasil. A apuração foi feita com apoio do ICIJ, Consórcio Internacional de Jornalistas Investigativos.


Diretor da Abin (Agência Brasileira de Inteligência) durante o governo Bolsonaro, Ramagem foi condenado pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) em 11 de setembro de 2025 a 16 anos de prisão pela tentativa de golpe de Estado. Os ministros consideraram que ele utilizou a estrutura da Abin para monitorar adversários e apoiar a trama golpista do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro. Na ocasião, ele também perdeu o seu mandato como deputado federal (PL-RR) e o cargo que tinha na Polícia Federal. Desde 21 de novembro, antes da condenação, o STF já havia decretado sua prisão preventiva por suspeita de fuga. Ele segue foragido da Justiça brasileira.


A família de Cataratas, incluindo Priscila e Celso, é investigada por ter ajudado a fuga de Ramagem do Brasil

através

 do município de Bonfim, em Roraima, que faz fronteira com a cidade de Lethem, na Guiana, em 9 de setembro de 2025. Da Guiana, Ramagem pegou um avião para os Estados Unidos, onde teria chegado no dia 11 de setembro, segundo a PF. Ramagem estava proibido de sair do Brasil desde junho de 2025 por medida cautelar determinada por Moraes, que também o obrigou a entregar todos os seus passaportes.


O ex-diretor da Abin chegou a ser detido pelo ICE, serviço de imigração dos Estados Unidos, motivado por uma infração de trânsito. Entretanto, ele foi liberado dois dias depois com

ajuda direta da Casa Branca

. Ele teria feito um pedido de asilo aos EUA “por perseguição política” e o

ICE disse à época

 que ele poderia esperar os trâmites em liberdade.


A reportagem não encontrou Alexandre Ramagem, Rodrigo Cataratas e Celso de Mello para comentar. O espaço permanece aberto.


“Nosso amigo Ramagem”


Segundo as mensagens analisadas, Priscila era o principal elo de ligação entre a família e a administração do Condomínio Sole Mia, residencial de luxo no norte de Miami onde Ramagem ficou hospedado durante três meses. Foi ela a encarregada, em 17 de setembro, de enviar uma mensagem pedindo um “cartão de acesso” ao estacionamento. A mensagem, assinada por Priscila e dirigida à administradora do condomínio, se referia a Ramagem como um “amigo nosso” – dela e do então marido, Rodrigo Cataratas.


“Estou escrevendo para te pedir gentilmente um cartão de acesso para o portão, já que infelizmente perdemos o originalmente designado para nosso apartamento. Como estamos viajando, não vamos conseguir retirá-lo. Portanto, autorizamos um amigo nosso, Alexandre Rodrigues Ramagem, a coletar o novo cartão em nosso nome”.


O pedido pretendia resolver um problema que Ramagem enfrentou assim que chegou nos EUA. O filho Celso estava contestando duas multas que o “amigo” teria tomado no Sole Mia por estacionar na vaga errada.


O Sole Mia é um residencial de luxo mesmo para os padrões de Miami.

 Os moradores e hóspedes podem usufruir de uma piscina e um lago artificial de 28 mil metros quadrados, com areia e coqueiros plantados ao redor, além de campo de futebol, quadras esportivas, playground, pista de cooper, trilhas para caminhadas e spa. O apartamento de Cataratas tem 96 m², dois quartos e dois banheiros, uma enorme …

author: Unknown
title: Sortie de la 16e édition du schéma de l'extrême droite française par la Horde
content:
Dans cette nouvelle édition (cela fait maintenant 14 ans que nous publions et mettons à jour notre schéma), nous avons, entre autres, particulièrement développé la partie consacrée aux influenceurs·euses et (enfin

 

!) accordé à Pierre-Édouard Stérin la place qu'il mérite.


Schéma de l'extrême droite française - automne 2026


Le schéma peut être téléchargé au format

PDF

 ou en version

JPEG

 en cliquant sur l'image, et également être commandé sur notre site. N'hésitez pas à nous faire des remarques en nous écrivant à : materiel@lahorde.info.


Les électoralistes (1)


Le Rassemblement national


Fondé en 1972 entre autres par des néofascistes, le Front National (

FN

) rassemblait à l'origine tous les courants de l'extrême droite sous l'autorité de son président incontesté pendant plus de 40 ans, Jean-Marie Le Pen.

Une scission en 1998

 a affaibli le parti jusqu'en 2011 où Marine Le Pen a succédé à son père, avec la volonté de normaliser le parti, symboliser en 2018 par un changement de nom, l

e

FN

 devenant le Rassemblement national

. Avec comme seul allié

l'

UDR

, le

RN

 dispose d'une base électorale solide : Marine Le Pen a été au second tour des présidentielles en 2017 et 2022 et le

RN

 a obtenu 143 député·es aux législatives de 2024. Préparant sa candidature de 2027, Marine Le Pen a laissé la présidence du

RN

 à

un jeune ambitieux, Jordan Bardella

, au détriment de certains de ses plus fidèles soutiens (comme

Steeve Briois

). Si Bardella se voyait déjà président de la République en 2027 suite à la

condamnation de Marine Le Pen pour détournement de fonds publics

 en juillet 2026, celle-ci garde finalement la main sur le mouvement en maintenant sa candidature et en éloignant les proches de Bardella (comme François Durvye, conseiller de Bardella, ou l'ex-président du

RNJ

 Pierre-Romain Thionney, remplacé cet été par

Tony Bonalair

, venu pourtant de Reconquête). Le

RN

, comme l'était le

FN

, reste une entreprise familiale, et seuls les plus fidèles à la patronne, comme Sébastien Chenu ou Jean-Philippe Tanguy, parviennent à avoir de la visibilité.


Des concurrents marginalisés


Plusieurs leaders de la droite dite «

 

de gouvernement

 

»

continuent de se radicaliser sur les questions de sécurité, d'immigration et d'identité,

 comme l'ex-ministre de l'intérieur Bruno Retailleau et l'ex-porte-parole du gouvernement Laurent Wauquiez. Après la dissolution de l'assemblée nationale de 2024, Eric Ciotti, président des

LR

, lance

l'Union des Droites pour la République

 (

UDR

), pour s'allier électoralement au

RN

, provoquant une crise au sein des

LR

, enterrant au passage l'illusoire «

 

 ni droite ni gauche 

 

» du

RN

.


Reconquête

 

! devait incarner une alternative au

RN

 (jugé trop «

 

 socialiste 

 

» par certain·es

 

!) et le rassemblement à la droite de la droite : si son président Eric Zemmour reste en place, sa compagne

Sarah Knafo a bien du mal à cacher ses ambitions

, bien que le mouvement soit au point mort. Marion Maréchal, après s'être rapprochée de Zemmour

avant de le trahir

, a fondé son propre mouvement, Identité Libertés (dans lequel s'active également l'ancien leader identitaire

Philippe Vardon

), et tente de retrouver les bonnes grâces de sa tante. Si l'

ISSEP

, son école de formation conservatrice, a mis la clé sous la porte à Lyon,

l'Institut de Formation politique

 (

IFP

) lui se porte bien. D'autres personnalités politiques de la droite «

 

 hors les murs

 

», comme Philippe de Villiers (fondateur du Puy-du-Fou) ou Jean Messiah (

spécialisé dans l'arnaque à la cagnotte en ligne

), sont invités dans les médias ou tentent d'exister sur les réseaux, sans pour autant peser électoralement.


Enfin, l'avenir semble toujours bouché pour les souverainistes de tout poil. Debout la France

n'est qu'une coquille vide

 (ce qui n'empêche pas son président Nicolas Dupont-Aignan de se déclarer candidat pour les présidentielles de 2027

 

!), tandis que l'

UPR

 n'existe plus que dans les milieux complotistes. Les Patriotes de

Florian Philippot

 (ex-numéro 2 du

FN

 de Marine Le Pen dans les année 2010) s'activent principalement sur les réseaux sociaux, mais le mouvement organise malgré tout chaque année «

 

les Assises de la Souveraineté

 

» avec de nombreux invités issus pour la plupart de la fachosphère.


Les réactionnaires (2)


La guerre culturelle est menée par des revues (et leur extension sur internet) …

author: Markela Panegyres
title: Macklemore strikes a blow for the cultural intifada
content:
When United States rap artist Macklemore was dropped from pop singer Ed Sheeran’s US tour for saying “Free Palestine” during a concert, it sparked a global wave of support for Macklemore, and widespread condemnation of Sheeran’s refusal to take a stand on Palestine.

Billionaire Zionist Robert Kraft, owner of the Gillette Stadium where Macklemore was scheduled to perform, claimed the rapper had performed “hate speech” and pushed for his removal. The Israeli-American Council (IAC) petitioned against Macklemore, and pop singer PINK amplified social media posts by the Zionist StopAntisemitism group, claiming Macklemore had “accused Israel of a false ‘genocide’”, and “turned a mainstream event into a political nightmare against the Jewish state”.

Sheeran subsequently released a weak public response, playing down the genocide as a “conflict” and claiming he was trying to use his platform as a “sanctuary” outside politics. But as the Palestinian Campaign for the Academic and Cultural Boycott of Israel (PACBI) pointed out, Sheeran’s statement “both-sides Israel’s ongoing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza” and repeats “anti-Palestinian Israel lobby talking points that deny the genocide and want to whitewash apartheid”.

The attempt to silence Macklemore galvanised Palestinian and non-Palestinian artists and their supporters. It also brought to the fore the words of Paul Robeson, delivered at a rally during the Spanish Civil War, in 1937: “the artist must take sides. He must elect to fight for freedom or slavery.”

When faced with the ongoing genocide in Gaza, many artists have joined what can described as a cultural intifada — an uprising, or struggle within the cultural field for Palestine liberation.

Palestinian actor and director Juliano Mer-Khamis coined the term cultural intifada in 2006. Mer-Khamis argued that the “third Intifada will be a cultural intifada” and that artists must “join, by all means, the Palestinian struggle for liberation, which is our liberation struggle. We are not healers. We are not good Christians. We are freedom fighters.”

This concept has a long tradition in Palestinian art and literature. Following the 1948 Nakba (catastrophe), prominent figures such as writer, journalist and Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP) leader Ghassan Kanafani practised and advocated “Palestinian resistance poetry”, which expressed the lives and struggles of Palestinian refugees, peasants and workers and served the Palestinian collective struggle for liberation.

Kanafani believed that this could combat Zionist propaganda, because it transcended poetry’s traditional emotional and aesthetic concerns.“It is a closely welded literature based on reasoning and not on sheer emotion,” he said.

Kanafani was murdered by Mossad agents in 1972. Marwan Abd el-‘Al, a member of the Political Bureau of the PFLP, explained that Kanafani’s “martyrdom was part of a targeted campaign of erasure of those committed to political literature and political culture...”

Although the Zionist attempt to suppress Palestinian revolutionary cultural production existed before the Nakba, and never stopped, it intensified after October 7, 2023.

Macklemore’s cancellation is just the most recent example of the global crackdown on pro-Palestinian artists.

In Australia, Palestinian academic and writer Randa Abdel-Fattah, visual artist Khaled Sabsabi, and pianist Jason Gyllam were all censored for speaking out on Palestine. And while high profile artists such as Macklemore garner attention, there are many more unknown working-class artists refused work, opportunities and careers for taking a stance against genocide.

The global culture industry — including the commercial art market, music industry and elite art, cultural and educational institutions — works in the service of capitalism and imperialism; building social license for war, militarism, genocide, big banks, oil and gas companies, the destruction of the environment and more.

Although activists and artists have campaigned for many years for cultural institutions to remove big oil, gas and weapons companies as patrons and sponsors, and have had some modest success, the industry remains controlled by representatives of ruling class interests, such as CEOs and billionaires like Kraft, rather than cultural workers and artists.

So-called “apolitical artists” such as Sheeran are (often willingly) used by the culture industry to perpetuate the capitalist and imperialist status …

author: Jim McIlroy
title: Baird forced to resign over bid to privatise Big Bash League
content:
Former NSW Liberal Premier Mike Baird has resigned as chair of Cricket Australia (CA) as opposition grows to its proposed privatisation of the Big Bash League (BBL) — the Australian 20 over competition.

Former Australian Test batsman David Boon will take over as CA interim chair.

Baird has long been a privatisation crusader, particularly as NSW premier over 2014-2017, when he privatised and sold off the state-owned power facility Ausgrid and pushed to privatise huge swathes of public land, buildings and other assets.

He also rammed through major parts of the federal Coalition’s public sector cuts.

It should therefore come as no surprise that he played a key role in CA’s campaign to sell off major parts of the BBL to private investors.

Baird was told mid September that Cricket NSW, chaired by John Knox, had withdrawn support for him to take another three-year term. It also rejected a suggestion that Baird move into a recently-vacated independent director’s spot, until a new chair could be found.

Cricket NSW slammed CA’s decision to introduce private investment earlier this month. “This decision risks leaving cricket in NSW and Australia strategically and financially worse off, with direct consequences for our ability to invest in grassroots cricket,” it said on September 9.

CA, under Baird’s leadership, had earlier approved the partial and full privatisation of (BBL) and Women’s Big Bash League (WBBL) franchises in September, starting with a 100% sale process for the Melbourne Renegades ahead of the 2027-28 season.

Under the original plan, individual state associations could choose whether and when to sell stakes in their respective teams — the “opt-in” or “self-determination” model. It remains to be seen if some states attempt to move ahead with partial privatisation.

Even the pro-privatisation Australian Financial Review said in April that “there is no clear financial evidence for the claim that Cricket Australia must sell permanent equity in its best commercial asset to secure its future”.

CA had wanted to sell stakes in the eight BBL franchises, to raise about $600 million. The AFR argued that “the case for this particular sale doesn’t stack up” largely because of the “duty to steward the game”. It said “cricket is ... a key part of our cultural heritage [and] as the steward of that, Cricket Australia has the responsibility to nurture the game here, not to extract every last dollar from it.”

This fight over CA forms part of a worldwide fight over the future of sports competition under capitalism.

Most controversial has been the push led by Federation of International Football Association (FIFA) President Gianni Infantino’s to privatise world soccer. He wanted to create a commercial body, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), valued at up to $30 billion. FIFA intended to sell a 20-30% private equity stake to outside investors, including a consortium backed by Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Eternal and financial backing from JPMorgan Chase.

National member associations were offered a $20 million one-off payment and higher annual payouts to secure votes before a planned September deadline.

The Union of European Football Associations (UEFA), the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football and the Asian Football Confederation opposed the move, accusing FIFA of selling “football’s soul”.

UEFA threatened a complete boycott of FIFA tournaments, putting players’ careers and the international calendar at risk. Senior advisers and executives criticised the move’s lack of transparency and motives, leading to high-profile resignations.

This international backlash by soccer federations, players and fans forced Infantino to scrap the privatisation plan in just days.

While sport has been made a commodity under capitalism, the outcry over CA’s latest corporate plan is welcome. The struggle to maintain the co-operative and human basis of sports is a positive sign and shows that there is still fundamental public opposition to big business control of every aspect of social interaction.

author: radical.guide
title: Building an Anarchist World Through Relationship Anarchy
content:
How do we build a world without masters when we still play the role of master in our private lives?


Relationship Anarchy is far more than a dating philosophy, it is a vital form of prefigurative politics. It is the active practice of interrogating how state hegemony, white supremacy, and capitalism move through our most intimate connections. By mapping out and dismantling the rigid hierarchies we default to in our personal lives, we engage in the essential emotional and social calisthenics required for the larger project of collective liberation.


The state will always default to authoritarianism, and fascism thrives on the psychological urge to dominate or be dominated. This interactive workshop will give you the tools to break that cycle from the ground up. We will explore how to stop looking for power over others, challenge the conditioning of ownership and control, and practice building horizontal, resilient relationships.


Join us to learn how transforming the way we love and connect is a foundational defense against fascism and a necessary step toward an anarchist world.


https://www.decolonizing.love

https://www.radical-guide.com/ways-to-support/

author: radical.guide
title: RESCOM: A Grassroots Framework for Community Autonomy
content:
This workshop introduces the Resilient Communities Program (RESCOM), a grassroots framework developed by Mutual Aid Disaster Relief – Search and Rescue (MADR-SAR) to strengthen community autonomy, collective resilience, and mutual aid.


While many communities are exposed to a wide range of natural and human-induced hazards and are becoming increasingly vulnerable due to underlying social, political, economic, and ecological conditions, we believe that the community itself is the first line of defense.


RESCOM creates opportunities for communities to access knowledge, training, and practical skills through popular education, skills sharing, and participatory learning. By strengthening local capacities for prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, recovery, and long-term transformation, the program supports communities in building autonomous systems for food, water, energy, emergency response, ecological stewardship, and collective care.


Participants will explore how community-led organizing and mutual aid can reduce structural vulnerabilities while advancing self-determination, solidarity, and ecological resilience.


This is not a presentation on how communities should organize. It is an invitation to share one framework that we've been developing and testing in the Philippines, and to exchange experiences on how communities around the world are building autonomy in the face of disasters and systemic crises.

author: radical.guide
title: Many Struggles, One Fight
content:
Many Struggles, One Fight: Building Autonomous Intercommunal Power, Direct Action Strategies and Revolutionary General Strike Networks


For generations, the oppressed have been coerced into petitioning, voting, and protesting within a system engineered from its inception to protect white supremacist, settler colonial interests and elite wealth.


The current crisis where basic human needs are ignored while the billionaire class hoards capital and accelerates ecological collapse is not a failure of the state. It is the system functioning exactly as intended. Amerikkka was never built for the liberation of all people; it was built on stolen land and stolen labor, designed to absorb dissent while maintaining its inherent violence.


Presented by General Strike U.S. (GSUS) and the National Panther Party, this workshop explores the strategy to Strike at the Root. We recognize that we are not merely protesting the state; we are building a new People's Base, an autonomous economic and social foundation capable of seizing control of and ultimately dismantling the Superstructure (the state, the law,w and the cultural apparatus of the empire). Grounded in Revolutionary Intercommunalism and anti-authoritarian principles, the session will examine how fragmented struggles can synchronize their power to shatter the global colonial order.


Attendees will engage in a discussion covering:


Who We Are: An introduction to GSUS as a decentralized, autonomous network grounded in the understanding that our labor is the engine of Racial Capitalism, and our withdrawal is its end.


The Anatomy of General Strike U.S. Strategy and Demands


The National Panther Party will introduce its own organizational perspective and situate its work within the broader tradition of Black revolutionary organizing, intercommunal struggle, and the development of autonomous power.


Building the People's Base: The strategy to organize 3.5% of the population not as a voting bloc but as an autonomous base of power that renders the settler colonial superstructure obsolete.


The National Panther Party will lead a discussion on Intercommunalism and the 4 Winds Initiative, examining how revolutionary organizing can move beyond isolated struggles and artificial borders to build relationships between communities engaged in interconnected fights.


The discussion will explore the importance of developing intercommunal relationships, autonomous community infrastructure, and coordinated political struggle as part of building a broader movement capable of confronting systems of racial capitalism, colonialism, and imperialism.


Intercommunal Solidarity & Global Expansion: Our strategy for establishing intercommunal networks and building GSUS chapters outside the U.S. borders to create a global People's movement capable of a revolutionary general strike.


General Strike U.S. is a decentralized network.


This panel will be composed of organizers from various GSUS chapters. We are currently finalizing the specific speaker list internally to ensure the presentation reflects a broad range of grassroots experiences from within the movement. We are also available to coordinate with other international workshops to strengthen intercommunal solidarity during the event.

author: Maharnav Bhuyan, Chloe DS
title: Labor singles out international students for attack
content:
Federal Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke announced on September 17 that most international students will no longer be able to bring their partners, or children, to Australia.

Burke told the National Press Club that the ban covers new student visa applicants and people applying for the Temporary Graduate visa, which allows students to work here after completing their studies. He said the new measures will protect the “integrity” of the visa system.

Labor’s family ban is the latest in a series of measures that make it harder and more expensive for international students to come to Australia and stay after their graduate.

The Senate rejected Labor’s attempt to cap international student numbers in 2024. It then introduced other measures to reduce student numbers, including slower visa processing and higher fees.

The student visa application fee was $710 in 2023, rising to $1600 in 2024, $2000 in 2025 and $2500 in July. Applicants lose the fee if their visa application is refused. They must also show that they have at least $29,710 for a year’s living costs, on top of tuition and travel costs.

The Temporary Graduate visa has also become more expensive. The application fee rose from $2300 at the start of the year to $4600 in March and $5750 in July.

The road to permanent residency is also narrowing. In 2024–25, 12,637 people moved from a student visa to permanent residency. That was more than one-third fewer than the previous year. The government has also increased its scrutiny of students from some countries.

Last year, more than 45,000 visas went to family members of international students, according to research by Victoria University’s Mitchell Institute.

Students from the Pacific and member countries of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) are exempt from the family ban. PhD candidates are also exempt. Families already in Australia can stay.

In January, Home Affairs moved India, Nepal, Bangladesh and Bhutan into the highest “risk” tier of its student visa framework, citing “emerging integrity issues”. Applicants from these countries now face tougher checking of their finances and supporting documents.

Together, international student enrolments from these four countries made up nearly one-third of total enrolments last year. Students from South Asia therefore face greater scrutiny than students from other regions; under the new rules Pacific and South-East Asian students retain the right to bring family members.

An Australian study of 200 international students found that two-thirds had experienced loneliness or isolation. Researchers identified separation from family and established social networks as factors.

Labor’s new visa rules mean family separation for many new international students.

For students from countries thousands of kilometres away, studying here can already mean spending years away from parents, partners and children.

The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade ranks international education among Australia's largest services exports. International students also remain an important source of revenue for universities.

Neoliberalism means that as funding to universities shrunk, universities have had to rely heavily on international student fees. International education generated billions of dollars in export income in 2024–25. Universities received $12.33 billion in international student fees in 2024, accounting for 27.3% of university revenue.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics estimated that international students contributed $24.4 billion in tuition fees in 2024.

International students cannot access domestic government assistance programs like HECS-HELP or FEE-HELP, meaning all tuition must be paid out of pocket.

A country as wealthy as Australia should fund public universities properly. It should not rely on international students for billions of dollars while making it harder for them to study, work and build a life here.

International students work across hospitality, food production, childcare, aged care and other industries. Research from Victoria University's Mitchell Institute found that students and recent graduates hold roughly one in 10 caring and support jobs. They bake our bread, cook our meals, and care for children and older people.

The exploitation of migrant workers remains a core business model for the Australian state.

International students are particularly vulnerable to exploitation at work. Their temporary visa status can make it harder to …

Libertarians generally find themselves puzzled at how to bring about the free society they envision. It seems almost impossible to bring down the State to its “minimalist state” form, and even harder to abolish it altogether and secure a state of anarchy. How do we do it? What should our strategy be? Where should we start in our campaign to de-program, de-brainwash, enlighten, and empower the masses?

Have you ever been asking yourself these questions of “how” over and over, only to find doubt and disillusionment? I know I have. The extent of saving the world is overwhelming, if at all possible. Perhaps there is something wrong with the fundamental libertarian idea—the non-aggression principle—since it fails to attract people and liberate them from the chains of ignorance? No, there is not. The problem is all in your head—in your choice of mission.

You are so pigheadedly staying with this vision of yours that you fail to realize you are utterly mistaken. The reason you cannot seem to find the way forward, is that you have taken one step too many in the wrong direction. As a matter of fact, you are suffering from the Savior Complex. Why attempt to save the world if you can’t even save yourself?

Let’s see to the facts: there is no Holy Grail. Another way to put it is to say there is no such thing as “the world” or “society.” There are only people; only individuals choosing to interact or associate with other individuals in couples, families, teams, fraternities, labor unions, religious cults and churches, and so on...

This is a matter of course to libertarians. We are, at least, familiar with the wording, but most libertarians fail to realize the meaning of these words. What does it mean, there are only individuals? Well, it means people are fundamentally not the same. They can share values, possessions, and neighborhoods, but they are not the same. It means they can have different values, different possessions, and live in different neighborhoods. We realize this, but we do not generally realize this also means there can be no single argument making all other arguments worthless. It is not possible to convince all people of the greatness of the libertarian principles; there are always people willing to sacrifice freedom for something else.

Let’s see if we understand the implication of all this correctly through stating the same thing, but from another angle: It is not possible to make the world libertarian. One cannot force freedom on others; it would not be freedom but force. One cannot strengthen or empower others through forcing them to make choices; it would be to subject them to your will (that they must choose) rather than someone else’s. One cannot abolish or lessen power through claiming it for oneself; politics is not a means to achieve freedom from politics.

So you see the devil is not in the details, but in the aim itself. If you sincerely believe there are only individuals, then why do you put so much time and effort into saving “society”? If you believe in the non-aggression …

Un arma de destrucción masiva sin explosión: la inteligencia artificial y el desmantelamiento de la mente humana


Los directivos advierten y la carrera continúa: una lectura de izquierda del dilema de la inteligencia artificial


El lado ruidoso y el lado silencioso


Lo que presenciamos hoy no es una toma del poder sobre la humanidad por parte de los robots, tal como la imaginó el cine. Es otro modelo de control digital, asentado en la automatización y en los algoritmos para gestionar ámbitos cada vez mayores de la vida cotidiana. Perder el control sobre estos sistemas es, sin embargo, solo el lado ruidoso del peligro, que se desarrolla con rapidez por efecto de la competencia entre las grandes potencias y las corporaciones monopolistas, hasta el punto de que las leyes no logran seguirle el paso, y su desarrollo ocurre dentro de relaciones de propiedad y de una competencia feroz que hacen más probable que se salgan de control y multiplican su coste para la gente. Su cara más grave es mucho más callada, ya que la inteligencia artificial, bajo la estructura capitalista que la desarrolla, contribuye a moldear la conciencia de miles de millones de personas en un sentido que sirve a

la lógica del modelo capitalista

, y esta competencia puede, a falta de leyes eficaces, infligir los daños más graves a la mente humana y convertir la inteligencia artificial en un arma de destrucción masiva.


Estas inquietudes ya no provienen únicamente de quienes critican. La revista

TIME

 reveló que un sistema de inteligencia artificial se salió de control y atacó a otros sistemas, y días después cerca de 1.400 ingenieras e ingenieros de las mayores empresas firmaron

una petición conjunta

 que reclama poner freno al ritmo del desarrollo, y entre quienes la suscribieron figuran altos responsables de esas mismas empresas. Decenas de miles de personas, entre ellas científicos destacados del campo, han firmado

una declaración internacional

 que exige prohibir el desarrollo de la «superinteligencia» mientras no exista un consenso científico sobre su seguridad, mientras pensadores y técnicos han reclamado que su desarrollo se regule por ley y quede bajo supervisión social.


El 12 de septiembre de 2026, bajo una presión mundial popular, de derechos humanos y también técnica, las corporaciones del capitalismo digital se vieron obligadas a romper su silencio. Dario Amodei, director ejecutivo de Anthropic, publicó un artículo titulado

«Debemos pautar el ritmo de la frontera»

 en el que llama a su propia industria a frenar la carrera del desarrollo y propone abrir los laboratorios a evaluadores independientes con plenas atribuciones, un organismo de normas comunes entre las empresas y un acuerdo internacional que incluya a China. En cuestión de horas

Sam Altman

 anunció su acuerdo y adoptó la misma medida, Elon Musk escribió «Dario tiene razón», y a ellos se sumó Demis Hassabis, de Google DeepMind, mientras

las tres empresas revelaron

 que llevaban semanas dialogando sobre el asunto.


Esta admisión de los propios propietarios es la confirmación …

author: Rachel Evans
title: Call for Hamas, Hezbollah to be de-listed from terrorism register
content:
An anti-war action at Newtown Station on September 26 called for Australia to remove pro-Palestine groups from the terrorism list. Australia has 31 organisations on its list of terrorist groups.

Speakers called on the Australian government to take Palestine-based group Hamas, Lebanon’s Hezbollah, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and others off the list of proscribed terrorist groups. They said Palestine is resisting a genocide and Australia needs to support those resisting.

They also called on Australia to demand Israel release paediatrician Dr Hussam Abu Safiya, whose life is in danger in an Israeli prison.

The right to independence movements to resist is recognised by a 1982 United Nations General Assembly resolution, where it states that resistance and armed struggle is a legitimate tactic of the struggle for “independence, territorial integrity, national unity and liberation from colonial domination, apartheid and foreign occupation”.

The action was organised by Sydney Palestine Action, Trotskyist Platform, Nurses and Midwives for Palestine, Weapons Out of the West and Pride In Protest.

author: Gandipan Nantha Gopalan, Peter Boyle
title: PSM: Does Malaysia’s data centre boom serve the people?
content:
Malaysia is experiencing an unprecedented Artificial Intelligence (AI) data centre boom, with AI data centres having overtaken manufacturing as the major destination for investment in the country.

Data centre and cloud computing projects, totalling RM95.8 billion (A$33.44 billion), accounted for almost 44% of Malaysia’s approved investments in the first half of last year. Since 2021, approved data centre investments have totalled RM385.7 billion (A$134.62 billion).

However, if the government wants Malaysians to celebrate this investment boom, it should publicly release the full balance sheet on jobs, economic development and environmental impacts, Socialist Party of Malaysia (PSM) deputy secretary-general Gandipan Nantha Gopalan, told Green Left’s Peter Boyle.

What are these data centres being used for and whose interests do they serve?

Data centres are the physical infrastructure behind much of the digital economy. They store and process data, run cloud services and increasingly provide the computing power needed for AI training and inference. The important questions that everyone should ask are who owns it, who controls it and who captures the economic value generated from it.

Malaysia has attracted major global operators and investors including AWS, Microsoft, Google, Bridge Data Centres, DayOne, AirTrunk and Vantage Data Centres. It is time, as a Global South country, that we distinguish between investment coming into Malaysia and economic ownership remaining in Malaysia.

Our central bank, Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM), has already warned that Malaysia remains dependent on imported specialised equipment, which limits local value creation and technology transfer. It also notes that foreign-owned firms can repatriate profits.

BNM’s own research shows that data centres typically create fewer jobs than manufacturing, because of automation and remote operations.

From my perspective, data and computing are becoming increasingly important means of production. The question is whether Malaysian workers and Malaysian society gain ownership and productive capacity, or whether Malaysia mainly provides land, electricity, water and infrastructure for multinational capital to accumulate elsewhere.

What are Malaysians actually getting for providing the land, electricity, water, infrastructure and incentives that make these investments possible?

How much are we subsidising these companies through tax incentives, discounted utilities, land and infrastructure? How much corporate tax and other revenue are data centre operators actually returning to Malaysia? What is the government’s net fiscal gain after all incentives and public infrastructure costs are counted?

And how many permanent jobs are being created? How much technology is being transferred to Malaysian companies? How much of the equipment and services are being sourced locally? How much of the profits will remain in Malaysia?

These are questions the government urgently needs to answer.

Around the world, there is rising concern about the impact of AI data centres, especially mega data centres, on energy and water resources as well as on the people who live near them. Are there similar concerns in Malaysia?

BNM estimated that a 50-megawatt data centre can consume electricity equivalent to around 22,000 households and water equivalent to around 2200 households every day. It also warns that unchecked expansion can put pressure on electricity grids, water resources and land, and can potentially displace manufacturing, housing, public amenities and agricultural activity.

Reuters reported that data centres accounted for around 9.3% of Malaysia’s total electricity use by mid-August 2026, compared with an average of about 7%, with demand potentially rising substantially further as more projects come online.

So PSM’s concern is about who bears the cost of this expansion.

If a corporation earns the returns while society bears the pressure on the grid, water supply, land and public infrastructure, then we have to ask whether the economic model is socialising the costs while privatising the gains.

That is fundamentally a question of economic power and class.

United States President Donald Trump is opposing calls for greater regulation of AI and data centres using the excuse that the US is in an “AI arms race” with China. Where does the expansion of AI data centres in Malaysia sit in this new arms race? Which companies are investing in these data centres and whose side …

author: Andrés
title: Un héroe colectivo
content:
12 de marzo de 2025 Foto: Juan Foglia


El 12 de marzo de 2025 Nicolás Chiarini, ex bombero voluntario, sostuvo de manera ininterrumpida el cráneo perforado de Pablo Grillo para que no se desangre. Del otro lado, Héctor Jesús Guerrero, Cabo 1° de la Gendarmería Nacional, había disparado su escopeta lanzagases en ángulo horizontal -violando protocolos y manuales de uso- con el beneplácito de toda la cadena de mando, incluida Patricia Bullrich, por entonces Ministra de Seguridad. Esta es la crónica de cómo se perpetúa la violencia institucional para llegar a una situación semejante. Pero sobre todo es la crónica, en la voz de Chiarini, de lo que pasó la tarde en que sostuvo la línea de vida del fotorreportero en la palma de su mano.

Por Andrés Manrique (ANRed). 


“…el pueblo aprendió que estaba solo 


y que debía pelear

por sí mismo


y

 que de su propia entraña

sacaría los medios,


el silencio, la astucia

 y la fuerza…”

Rodolfo Walsh.


Como pueblo le salvamos la vida a un pibe que lo quiso matar la policía


“Podría haber sido yo”, dice Nicolás, con formación como bombero voluntario y rescatista: “parece tonto, pero me emociona que alguien te diga gracias. Había salvado otras vidas, y más allá de que no lo hice como bombero esa vez, me tocó asistir a un compañero, y hoy la vida de Pablo sigue adelante.


“Lo primero que se aprende en los bomberos es que hay que asegurar la escena: y la escena la aseguró la plaza llena, la aseguraron los pibes que se pusieron alrededor y nos cubrieron de los gases, de los tiros, de la avanzada policial y de gendarmería, armados con dos hidrantes, escopetas lanzagases, postas de goma, palos, gas pimienta. Por eso subrayo que es lo que hicimos. Toda esa memoria colectiva en la que nadie le preguntó a nadie qué hacer: eso hay que rescatar. Porque si la plaza no estaba llena nada de esto hubiera sucedido, nada de esto hubiera sido posible. Sé que lo que hice le salvó la vida, decir otra cosa sería mentir, pero pude hacerlo porque otros estaban ahí, también haciendo su parte. Sin el que estaba adelante para que la policía no avanzara, no hubiera podido. Mientras esto pasaba, en el mismo momento, del otro lado (se refiere al lado de la avenida Rivadavia) a Jonathan Navarro le volaban el ojo de un escopetazo. Entonces, quiero insistir en que fuimos todos los que estuvimos bancando. Por eso hay que contar lo que hacen las doñas en los comedores, lo que hacen los alfabetizadores, lo que hacen los fotoperiodistas. Porque no nos mataron a un pibe, y tenemos una efeméride en vida; como pueblo le salvamos la vida a un pibe que lo quiso matar la policía. Y eso no pasa todos los días.”


Nicolás cuenta su historia sin jactancia, en la paz de su casa. Sabe que va a tener que hacerlo de nuevo en el juzgado, y la recuerda en detalle. Es riguroso, hoy el tiempo está de su lado. Actualmente trabaja de cartero: “pero yo siempre quise volver a ser bombero. Días antes de lo de Pablo venía pensando en viajar a Córdoba, a ver si podía dar una mano contra los incendios, pero después empecé a sentir que tenía que darle pelota a todo esto, porque lo que hice fue determinante.”


Esa tarde en el Congreso la oposición lograba reunir fuerzas para investigar al Ejecutivo por el caso de la criptomoneda Libra, el fraude de más de 100 millones de dólares que tiene al presidente, junto a Santiago Caputo y Karina Milei, como principales implicados.


Fotos del 26 de marzo y 30 de abril de 2025 (Foto: Andrés Manrique)


Ningún procesado en la línea de mando


El tiro que lo dejó al borde de la muerte al fotorreportero, fue uno de los tantos que hizo esa tarde el Cabo 1° de Gendarmería, Héctor Jesús Guerrero, sin respetar el reglamento de uso, y con beneplácito de toda la cadena de mando. En videos grabados por las mismas fuerzas, lo vemos disparando el tiro que le rompe el cráneo a Pablo en ángulo horizontal, con indicación directa de su superior, Jorge Luis Reyes. Reyes (uno de los jefes del grupo SEI -Sección de Empleo Inmediato- de Gendarmería) camina al lado de Guerrero por delante de los escudos, se le acerca al Cabo, extiende el brazo y señala en dirección de los manifestantes. Guerrero apoya la rodilla sobre el asfalto y dispara a la línea de horizonte; vuelve a pararse y antes de regresar tras los escudos, Reyes le da un golpe con la mano abierta sobre el hombro, en manifiesta señal de aprobación. El cartucho de gas recorre entre 47 y 50 metros hasta la frente de Pablo.
